meta.name: The Belligerent Five
whatWeKnow: Mara died after a brief recovery when moon-petal failed against a deeper corrupted force.
Moonfall Grotto is a temple of Selune and site of a lunar trial.
Seris forcibly attuned to the first artifact and the party saw five more linked relics.
Seris exposed her divine bloodline during the battle beneath the Vesperveil Crystal and has been named High Priestess of Lunaryth.
The Weeping Marsh is the nearest confirmed lead for another relic.
Edrin and Lyra were abducted because they knew about the Circle of Promise, but Edrin was later murdered in the inn ambush before the party reached the marsh.
Greyhaven is filling with organized newcomers and growing steadily more dangerous.
The Circle of Promise may hide a buried weapon that should never be unearthed.
Greyhaven contained a dismantled memorial being formally erased by robed civic agents tied visually to the Moonfall faction.
When the shrine was restored, the stones sang and Echo witnessed a vision of a calm drow cutting his palm over a blood basin in red firelight.
On the road into the Weeping Marsh, the party survived an inn-room massacre attempt, took three new guest allies with them, and cut down the Red Witness on the staked path.
The Circle of Promise opened only after blood was offered, and the Bloodbound Testament eventually passed from Echo to Prom, reshaping itself into a greataxe.

Deep in the Weeping Marsh, the party found the next artifact site, watched the marsh conjure false essences of Edrin and Lyra through the swamp, severed the roots tying them to the artifact, and saw the marsh artifact bind itself to Prom.
Kelsier is dead. His tortured body was thrown onto the path after the party left the Weeping Marsh, moments before robed attackers demanded Seris and the marsh artifact.

After leaving the marsh, robed attackers ambushed the party. Mead went down for the first time, but Prom's combination of the Tearstone and Bloodbound Testament let him purge magical influence and slaughter the ambushers before any useful information could be extracted.
On the road to Lunaryth, the party lost their gold to an old traveler in a game of road dice, then murdered him and took the gold back.
The party has reached Lunaryth and learned the Guild Games are happening in a few days.
The Mercantile League has won the last six Guild Games, hoards many of the best items in the city, and treated the party like peasants before kicking them out.
Mead found kindred spirits in the Civic Wardens, whose members seem to love brawling almost as much as he does.
Echo recognized the central statue in Lunaryth as Aelwyn Vaeloris, the woman from his visions.
Echo exposed Elyndor's false history and revealed that Aelwyn saved Lunaryth from the drow attacker.
Seris used Channel Divinity to break the drow's Shadow of Moil, allowing the nearly defeated party to prevail.
An ice dragon and a fire-and-lightning dragon are attacking Lunaryth, fulfilling Echo's vision of the burning city.
Prom now knows that the lightning strike from his childhood came from the fire-and-lightning dragon attacking Lunaryth.

editableSheet.backstory:
Kian Mehravan was born on the Saffron Coast, a homeland of sea wind, saffron markets, poetry, gardens, and old civic rites. Then the Iron Crescent seized power and called it purification. They claimed to defend faith and national virtue, but their rule became patrols, prisons, forced confessions, and fear.

Their first and most visible targets were women who refused to lower their eyes. Veil Patrols stopped women in streets and markets to inspect headscarves, hair, sleeves, voices, and who they walked beside. A loose scarf became rebellion. A public song became corruption. A student protest became treason. Women were dragged into wagons for correction while officials preached that cruelty was protection.

Kian's family resisted by hiding fugitives, smuggling prison names out of the coast, and exposing what the Iron Crescent did behind sacred banners. The Crescent answered with arrests, executions, threats against families, and confessions beaten into people before public display. Kian escaped because others stayed behind to buy him time.

Now he gathers strength in exile. He does not want a throne for its own sake. He wants enough power, allies, and proof to return to the Saffron Coast and break the Iron Crescent's hold. His greatest fear is not death. It is that hatred will make him into another man with soldiers, slogans, and prisons.

editableSheet.backstory:
U Turn is a rogue, smuggler, and professional bad influence from a far-off coastal land where the laws are strict, the ports are corrupt, and everyone insists they are just moving spices. He was banished after getting caught smuggling a forbidden narcotic paste called green hush inside crates of preserved avocados. His official sentence was exile. His version is: "Banishment is just travel with paperwork."

After being forced out, he drifted from port to road to border town, doing courier work, debt collection, and occasional inventory correction. He eventually ran into Duldrick and Kian on a bad stretch of road. Kian had been cornered by bandits, and Duldrick was already in the middle of saving him. U Turn, who had absolutely not been hiding nearby, saw an opportunity to rob the bandits while they were distracted. The plan lasted almost eight seconds. One shout, one thrown bottle, and one questionable knife later, U Turn had somehow become part of the rescue.

He now refers to the whole event as a three-way strategic intervention. He travels with Duldrick and Kian because he owes Duldrick for not letting the bandits kill him, thinks Kian is good luck in a bad way, and suspects the Belligerent Five are walking toward money, trouble, or both.

sessions.title: Session Zero — Ascendaria (Player Primer)
sessions.summary: Player primer and opening setup as the party sails toward Tide’s Rest en route to Lunaryth.

sessions.title: Bells in the Lost Forest
sessions.summary: The party learns of the Lost Forest's true danger, meets Seris in Tide’s Rest, and slays the undead cow that tolls the bells.

lowlight.name: Kelsier
lowlight.reason: Almost died from a combo of stupidity and bad luck, then shamelessly flirted with Seris while she tried to save her mother

sessions.title: Moonfall Trial and the Sealed Letter
sessions.summary: After Mara's death, the party pushed through the Lost Forest into Moonfall Grotto, survived a hostile robed faction and Selune's trial, and witnessed Seris attune to the first artifact before learning Elyndor is alive in Lunaryth.

mvp.name: Mead
mvp.reason: Brutally eliminated the robed leader, broke enemy morale, and swung the Moonfall fight tempo in the party's favor.

lowlight.name: Prom
lowlight.reason: Challenged Seris for the sealed letter, landed zero hits, got dusted in the duel, then smashed the robed leader's head and lost the planned Speak with Dead lead.

sessions.title: Roadside Thieves and the Greyhaven Hook
sessions.summary: After securing Moonfall's side-room weapons and saying goodbye to Seris, the party got robbed during a long-rest honeypot, spent most of a guest appearance bullying Aylin, tracked the thieves to a bandit camp, watched Prom commandeer a horse and trample the three thieves, then rescued Edrin and Lyra and learned about Greyhaven, the Weeping Marsh, and the Circle of Promise.

mvp.name: The Belligerent Five
mvp.reason: Tracked the thieves immediately, hit the bandit camp fists first, and rescued Edrin and Lyra before the situation could spiral.

lowlight.name: Mead & Echo
lowlight.reason: Brought the night visitors into their tent, ignored every red flag, and woke up lighter on coin and gear.

sessions.title: Greyhaven and the Singing Stones
sessions.summary: The party reached Greyhaven, antagonized half the inn, discovered robed officials finishing the erasure of a disputed memorial, fought to restore the shrine, and triggered a singing-stone vision that showed Echo a blood ritual performed by a calm drow in red firelight.

mvp.name: Echo
mvp.reason: Clocked the robed faction, pushed through the shrine restoration beat, and completed the melody that triggered the campaign's next major vision.

lowlight.name: Everyone's Dice
lowlight.reason: The session was a graveyard of natural 1s, failed dignity checks, and avoidable chaos before the shrine payoff finally landed.

sessions.title: Inn Ambush and the Red Witness
sessions.summary: What should have been a safer night at the inn turned into a brutal assassination opener that killed Edrin and dropped Echo almost immediately, but the party recovered, linked up with three new guest PCs, pushed down the staked path into the Weeping Marsh approach, and overwhelmed the Red Witness despite losing their stolen bandit prisoner to a clean decapitation.

mvp.name: The Extra Bodies
mvp.reason: The three guest PCs tilted the action economy hard enough that the Red Witness never really got to become the boss fight it wanted to be.

lowlight.name: Echo
lowlight.reason: Got shot down almost immediately in both major fights and kept burning Heat Metal into a single target hard enough to distort the entire encounter plan.

sessions.title: The Circle Opens and the Marsh Answers
sessions.summary: At the Circle of Promise, Mead and Echo blooded themselves to open the obelisk, Echo claimed the dagger inside, and Lyra died trying to stop him from wielding it. Echo later bequeathed the Bloodbound Testament to Prom, where it took the shape of a greataxe. From there MooMoo mapped the way into the Weeping Marsh, Mead plunged eighty feet down a well, touched the artifact, and triggered a brutal fight against marsh-conjured essences of Lyra and Edrin. Aylin, being a rogue, ran straight to the front to try to take the artifact and got her head bashed in by Lyra's legendary actions before Prom dealt heavy damage, the party severed the roots tying the false returns to the artifact, and the Tearstone attached itself to Prom.

mvp.name: Mead and Prom
mvp.reason: Mead bled for the obelisk, survived the eighty-foot drop, rushed the artifact first, and brought Aylin back after the fight went sideways. Prom dealt heavy damage throughout the marsh fight and walked away as the bearer of the Tearstone.

lowlight.name: Aylin
lowlight.reason: Tried to steal Echo's new knife, then later ran to the front like a rogue trying to grab the artifact and got her head bashed in by Lyra's legendary actions.

sessions.title: The Bearer Breaks the Ambush
sessions.summary: After leaving the Weeping Marsh, the party found Kelsier's tortured body thrown onto the path as robed attackers demanded Seris and whatever had been brought up from below. Mead was downed for the first time, Echo was nearly forced into danger by Crown of Madness, and Prom proved terrifyingly dominant as the Tearstone of the Waning Tide and Bloodbound Testament worked together to purge the charm before he could destroy Echo. The last attacker surrendered, but Prom could not resist finishing a weakened enemy and decapitated him before the party could extract answers. On the road to Lunaryth afterward, the party lost badly at road dice to an old traveler, then murdered him and took the gold back. They reached Lunaryth, learned the Guild Games were coming in a few days, visited the guilds, found Mead's kind of brawlers in the Civic Wardens, and got kicked out of the Mercantile League after learning the League hoards top-tier items and has won the last six Games. The session ended at the central statue, where Echo realized the woman carved there is the woman from his visions.

mvp.name: Prom
mvp.reason: The Tearstone and Bloodbound Testament made him overwhelming in the ambush: he resisted the worst consequence of Crown of Madness, purged the remaining attackers, and turned the fight decisively.

lowlight.name: The Belligerent Five
lowlight.reason: Prom killed a surrendered ambusher before questioning, and the party later murdered an old traveler after losing their gold to him in road dice.

sessions.title: The Statue Opens the Way
sessions.summary: Echo followed the melody etched into the central statue into a vision of ancient Lunaryth burning. The party then used the library and Red Light district to keep pushing through the city, found Seris at the statue, and learned her mother had once worked the Red Light. Under the Hall of Civic Records they uncovered the buried history of Lunaryth and a hidden shrine below the city, found a keepsake tied to Seris's mother, and saw the city's blackmail papers point directly at the star-touched twins rumor around her family. On the way out a black pendant cracked open, released a huge bound beast, and the party had to kill it before claiming the pendant as their own.

mvp.name: Echo
mvp.reason: The statue melody and vision did the heaviest story work of the session and opened the path into Lunaryth's buried history.

lowlight.name: Prom
lowlight.reason: The prayer circle and the blood-touched visions gave him less than he hoped, and the pendant-beast escape only made the item problem stranger.

sessions.title: Mead Wins the Guild Games
sessions.summary: The Guild Games reached their violent conclusion with Mead standing as champion. After the celebration and Moon Drop fallout, the party was invited to the finalists' reception and witnessed the Vesperveil Crystal demonstration, where the High Priest of Lunaryth was revealed as Elyndor Vaeloris. The crystal answered Echo's familiar melody, Elyndor's face carried an unmistakable resemblance to Seris, and the session ended as the room went dark.

mvp.name: Mead
mvp.reason: Won the Guild Games, turned Civic Warden brawling into citywide recognition, and became the party's public path into Lunaryth's highest circles.

lowlight.name: Lunaryth
lowlight.reason: The city dressed the party beautifully, applauded politely, then revealed that its highest priest is Elyndor Vaeloris while the Vesperveil Crystal began answering Echo's vision melody.

sessions.title: The Truth Burns and Dragons Descend
sessions.summary: At the Vesperveil Crystal demonstration, Echo shattered Elyndor's carefully staged story and revealed the truth of Aelwyn Vaeloris saving Lunaryth from the drow who had attacked it. Elyndor was exposed as a fraud, but the drow struck back and nearly wiped out the party beneath Shadow of Moil. Seris saved the fight with Channel Divinity, stripping away the darkness so the party could finally land their blows and win by the narrowest margin. After a long recovery, Seris was recognized as part of Lunaryth's divine bloodline and named High Priestess. The peace lasted only until two dragons descended on the city: one breathing ice, the other wielding fire and lightning. As Lunaryth burned exactly as Echo had seen, Prom realized the lightning strike from his childhood had come from the dragon now directly in front of him.

mvp.name: Seris
mvp.reason: Her Channel Divinity broke through Shadow of Moil when almost everyone was down, exposed the drow to the party's attacks, and turned a near-total defeat into a desperate victory.

lowlight.name: Elyndor Vaeloris
lowlight.reason: His public spectacle collapsed when Echo revealed the true history of Aelwyn and exposed the High Priest's version of Lunaryth's salvation as a fraud.

No birds. No insects.
Occasionally: a faint, distant bell
Players are explicitly aware that shadows cling unnaturally to trees and roots.
This is not hidden danger — it is ignored danger.
FOREST RULE: SHADOW CORRUPTION
🌑 Interacting with Shadows (Intentional Penalty)
If a player:
Touches the shadow itself
Cuts through it
Casts magic directly into it
Attempts to dispel or manipulate it
➡️ Immediate effect:
CON Save (DC 11)
Fail: 1d6 necrotic damage
Success: Half damage
Notes:
This can only trigger once per PC in the forest
The shadows recoil after harming someone
Make it clear the damage feels punitive, not aggressive
DM Tone:
“The shadow lashes back — not alive, but offended.”
This is not too mean for level 1 because:
It’s avoidable
It’s telegraphed
It’s capped
It teaches an important rule early
TRAVEL THROUGH THE FOREST (FIRST ENTRY)
Distance
Short but tense. No more than 15–20 minutes in-world.
Use 1–2 hazards total, not all.
🌲 HAZARD 1: SHADOW-SNAGGED BRANCH
Trigger:
 Moving too quickly, failing a Perception check, or pushing ahead without caution.
Effect:
DEX Save (DC 11)
Fail: Disadvantage on the PC’s next attack roll
Success: No effect
Flavor:
“A dead branch snaps — shadow clings briefly to your weapon hand.”
No damage. Tactical impact only.
🌑 HAZARD 2: GRASPING CANOPY
Trigger:
 Investigating sounds, bells, or pausing to listen.
Effect:
WIS Save (DC 10)
Fail: Disadvantage on Initiative OR next Perception check
Success: No effect
Flavor:
“For a moment, the forest feels closer than it should.”
This subtly benefits the ambush without announcing it.
🌲 OPTIONAL HAZARD 3: SHADOWED ROOTS (BEST USED ON 1 PC)
Trigger:
 Crossing the clearing near the Big Tree.
Effect:
STR or DEX Save (DC 11)
Fail: The PC does not have their reaction in round 1 of the next combat
Success: No effect
No damage. Strong tactical consequence.
THE BIG TREE CLEARING
Description
Massive, ancient tree
Bark split like scars
Roots exposed and blackened
Dead grass in a 10–15 ft radius
Shadows cling thickest here
Bells faintly audible, then silent
NPCs said the herb was “by the big tree.”
They were telling the truth.
🌿 THE HERB: MOONPETAL
Pale silver leaves
Softly luminescent
Grows at the base of the trunk
Clearly untouched by corruption
This gives a false sense of safety.
🌑 SHADOWLASH AURA (TREE INTERACTION)
If a PC:
Touches the tree
Harvests carelessly
Cuts bark
Casts magic at it
➡️ Trigger Shadowlash Aura (once total):
CON Save (DC 11)
Fail: 1d6 necrotic damage
Success: Half damage
After this:
Shadows withdraw slightly
The tree becomes inert
The ambush is imminent
🔔 FORESHADOWING THE AMBUSH
Give 2–3 signs before combat:
A low, distant moo
Massive hoofprints half-filled with water
A cracked bell tangled in roots
Birds abruptly going silent
Then silence.
Then impact.
🐄 ADMIRAL MOO MOO — AMBUSH
Trigger Conditions (Any One)
Moonpetal is harvested
Shadowlash Aura is triggered
Party lingers too long
MooMoo does not emerge from the tree — it charges from between the trees.
🌙🌲 THE LOST FOREST — SECOND TRAVERSAL (FINAL VERSION)
(Post-Mara’s Death • On the Way to Moonfall Grotto)
“The forest does not hunt you anymore.
 It waits.”
PURPOSE OF THIS TRAVERSAL
Show the forest has changed
Establish Guiding Bolt as a narrative key
Reinforce Seris’s importance without railroading
Penalize recklessness, not curiosity
Funnel the party cleanly into Moonfall Grotto
This should feel ritualistic, heavy, and inevitable.
ATMOSPHERE SHIFT (IMMEDIATE)
When the party re-enters the Lost Forest:
The bells ring once, distant and hollow — then stop
Shadows are thicker, but unmoving
The air is cold and still
Moonlight cuts through the canopy in narrow shafts
Make it clear:
This place is no longer testing them.
 It is judging.
THE SHADOW BARRIER
After several minutes of travel, the party encounters:
A wall of dense shadow spanning the path
It absorbs light and sound
It is physically impassable
It does not immediately attack
The way forward is blocked.
PLAYER CHOICES (LET THEM DRIVE)
Do not prompt the solution immediately.
Allow players to:
Attack the shadow
Cast spells
Investigate
Ask Seris for help
Each choice teaches something.
🌑 STUPIDITY PENALTY (INTENTIONAL, FAIR)
If a PC:
Attacks the shadow
Casts magic directly into it
Touches it recklessly
➡️ Shadow Reprisal
CON Save (DC 11)
Fail: 1d6 necrotic damage
Success: Half damage
Important Notes
This can trigger multiple times, but:
Do not stack it rapidly
One PC at a time
Describe it as punitive, not aggressive
“The shadow lashes back — not alive, but offended.”
SERIS INTERVENTION (NATURAL, NOT FORCED)
After one or two failed attempts, allow:
A player to ask Seris directly
Or Seris to speak up hesitantly
Suggested line:
“My mother said the moon doesn’t fight the dark… it shows it the way.”
She is unsure. Quiet. Afraid of being wrong.
✨ THE KEY: GUIDING BOLT (ONE USE ONLY)
If Guiding Bolt is cast at the shadow barrier:
The shadows recoil, peeling back like a curtain
Moonlight pours through briefly
The barrier dissolves completely
The spell deals no damage
No attack roll required
Spell slot is expended
This happens once.
No further barriers appear.
SERIS HEALING SAFETY VALVE
After the barrier falls:
Seris quietly heals any injured PCs
She does not comment on it
This prevents early punishment from snowballing
This keeps the moment instructional, not punitive.
NO OTHER HAZARDS (IMPORTANT)
On this traversal:
❌ No falling branches
❌ No ambushes
❌ No random damage
The danger here is choice, not attrition.
FOREST RESPONSE (SUBTLE FORESHADOWING)
As the path opens:
The forest pulls back slightly
Shadows thin
The bells do not return
Optional line:
“For a moment, the shadow leans toward Seris… then withdraws.”
Shar is watching.
ARRIVAL AT MOONFALL GROTTO
The trees thin unnaturally.
Stone replaces soil.
Moonlight touches the ground uninterrupted.
Seris stops.
“This is as far as the forest goes.”
End traversal.

documents.title: Tide's Rest
documents.content:
📘 TIDE’S REST — DM LOCATION GUIDE
Act 1, Chapter 0: Arrival at the Edge of the World
🌊 Overview of Tide’s Rest
Population: ~450
 Races: Mostly Human, Half-Elf, Gnome, a few Dwarves
 Tone:
Starving, isolated, fearful
Encroaching unnatural fog
Nights “too dark”
A sense that the sea and forest are wrong
Why this location matters:
 Tide’s Rest establishes the emotional stakes of the campaign and introduces Seris, Eldra, and the first major quest. Nothing here directly reveals Shar, Selûne, or the cosmic arc — it simply appears to be a town in decline.
🗺️ Town Layout Summary
(You already have your map — this ties NPC placement to it.)
Key Areas:
Shipyard/Docks – starting location
Moonwell Square – central hub, Seris encounter
Salted Kelp Tavern – gossip & rumors
Weary Lantern Inn – rest point & foreshadowing
Eldra’s Hut – quest hook
Forest Trail Gate – exit to Lost Forest
Lighthouse – optional eerie clue point
🧩 DM OBJECTIVES IN TIDE’S REST
By the time players leave Tide’s Rest, they should:
Care about Seris and her mother
Feel the town is suffering mysteriously
Understand the forest is dangerous
Have a clear direction: retrieve moonpetal from Moonfall Grotto
Be emotionally invested in leaving Tide’s Rest better than they found it
Learn the first hints about the shadows, without understanding them
Everything here supports those goals.
🌙 THE SERIS INTRODUCTION (Scripted Encounter)
Location: Moonwell Square
 Use: Introduces Seris, the emotional heart of the campaign
Scene Description (Read-Aloud)
The cracked crescent fountain at the center of Tide’s Rest trickles weakly. The square is quiet except for the wind scraping dry leaves across stone.
A young half-elf woman stands beside the fountain, clutching a satchel. Her eyes are red from lack of sleep.
She’s speaking urgently with a gnomish herbalist who seems entirely unmoved.
Seris (near tears, but composed):
“Please, Eldra… her fever is getting worse. You must have something left.”
Eldra (sharp, exhausted):
“Moonpetal grows in the Lost Forest, girl! And I’m not setting foot in there while a pale demon is breaking trees in half.”
Seris:
“Then… then what am I supposed to do?”
This is the moment the players naturally intervene.
🎭 ROLEPLAYING SERIS
Personality:
Soft-spoken but resilient
Deeply compassionate
Hides fear well
Not used to relying on others
Visible Traits:
Dark circles under her eyes
Worn clothes
Half-elven features softened by worry
A satchel with dried herbs, threadbare book, and a small carved charm
Motivations:
Save her mother
Avoid drawing attention to her lineage
Stay unnoticed
Push down growing dread about the forest and the moonwell
What she knows:
Her mother’s illness is worsening
Moonpetal may help
The forest has become unsafe
Locals whisper about “the pale beast”
Nothing about her father or brother (yet)
What she does not know:
Her celestial lineage
Her link to the artefacts
The cosmic crisis brewing
Why she feels “pulled” toward the forest edge
Why players won’t attack her:
She radiates vulnerability
She is polite, grateful, and helpful
She heals them later
She is clearly not a threat
Eldra scolds anyone who is rude to her
🧙 ROLEPLAYING ELDRA MOSSWHISTLE (Herbalist)
Tone: Abrupt, impatient, but caring beneath it
 Why she’s upset:
Supplies have run dry
The forest is deadly
She feels guilt about Seris’ mother but is too afraid to help
The town blames her for shortages
She’s at her breaking point
What she tells players:
“Moonpetal grows deep in the forest, near Moonfall Grotto. But that place is wrong now. Something’s twisting the woods.”
“If you insist on going, follow the old path — and don’t answer if you hear bells. Those aren’t bells.”
When asked about the pale creature:
“Big. White. Bones stickin’ out. Walks like it forgot how. Cracked a pine like a twig.”
(This sets up Admiral MooMoo beautifully.)
🍺 THE SALTED KELP TAVERN — NPCs & Rumors
NPC: Marda Bellowpot (Owner)
Loud, cheerful, always watching
Loves gossip
Slams mugs on tables with gusto
Treats Seris kindly, but worries for her
Rumors PC can learn (roll d6 or sprinkle naturally):
“A giant pale beast stalks the Lost Forest at night.”
“The lighthouse keeper swears he heard mooing in the fog.”
“The moonwell’s blessing has been fading for months.”
“Some say the forest is alive now. Breathing.”
“Strangers don’t come to Tide’s Rest anymore. You’re the first in ages.”
“Seris’ mother has been sick a long time… poor thing.”
Purpose of Tavern Rumors:
Foreshadow the forest danger
Build the MooMoo myth
Establish supernatural decay
Highlight the town’s isolation
🛏️ WEARY LANTERN INN — AMBIENT FORESHADOW
NPC: Odrin Fellbow (Innkeeper)
Nervous
Careful
Very observant
He tells PCs:
“Nights feel wrong lately. Too dark. Too quiet. Lanternlight doesn’t reach as far as it should.”
Night Encounter Atmosphere (no combat):
PCs hear distant cracking of a tree
Whispering wind with voices that aren’t words
A soft… distant moo
The forest line seems… closer
🧪 THE QUEST PROMPT: “Retrieve Moonpetal from Moonfall Grotto”
Eldra gives players:
A torn map scrap of the forest
A description of the herb
A warning that they’ll need to go very deep
Seris begs to help, but Eldra refuses to let her go — too dangerous.
Seris instead gives the party:
A small wooden charm (her mother's)
Quiet thanks
A promise to repay their kindness
📜 QUEST OBJECTIVES (DM ONLY)
Players should leave Tide’s Rest intending to:
Reach the Lost Forest
Track the forest path to Moonfall Grotto
Survive Admiral MooMoo
Acquire moonpetal
Return to Seris
Trigger the artefact awakening (end of Act 1)
🚪 THE FOREST TRAIL GATE
NPC: Rook Ashford (19, inexperienced guard)
Dialogue:
“If you hear mooing… don’t run. It gets excited.”
 “And if you hear bells? Gods help you — don’t answer.”
This scares them — but not too much.
🧍‍♂️ COMPLETE NPC LIST (Copy-Paste Clean Version)
Seris Vaeloris — Half-elf healer; emotional anchor; needs moonpetal
 Mara — Seris’ dying mother
 Eldra Mosswhistle — Herbalist; gives first quest
 Marda Bellowpot — Tavern owner; gossip hub
 Orrin Boatswain — Sailor who saw strange things
 Odrin Fellbow — Innkeeper; foreshadowing
 Captain Brecca Thornwhale — Shipmaster; exposition
 Rook Ashford — Young guard; forest warnings
 Jorin Crate-Boy — Teenage nuisance; light comic relief
 Lighthouse Keeper Orrick — Optional; says he heard mooing
 General Townsfolk — Scarce, fearful, hungry, superstitious
🧍 TIDE’S REST — QUICK NPC ONE-LINERS
Captain Brecca Thornwhale (Shipmaster)
Location: Docks
 One-liner:
“The sea won’t let ships leave anymore. Pushes them back like it’s alive.”
 Use: First hint that the isolation isn’t political or economic.
Marda Bellowpot (Tavern Owner)
Location: Salted Kelp Tavern
 One-liner:
“If the forest’s grown teeth, it ain’t my fault — but I’ll pour you a drink about it.”
 Use: Gossip delivery system and comic relief.
Orrin the Boatswain (Old Sailor)
Location: Salted Kelp Tavern
 One-liner:
“Saw a shadow under the waves bigger than my boat. Didn’t swim like anything natural.”
 Use: Sea of Spirals foreshadow.
Odrin Fellbow (Innkeeper)
Location: Weary Lantern Inn
 One-liner:
“Lanterns don’t push the dark back anymore. They just… sit in it.”
 Use: Night-time unease and atmospheric dread.
Rook Ashford (Young Guard)
Location: Forest Trail Gate
 One-liner:
“If you hear bells or mooing… don’t answer either.”
 Use: Forest danger warning + MooMoo setup.
Jorin ‘Crate-Boy’ Fen (Dock Teen)
Location: Docks / Market
 One-liner:
“They say the pale cow used to belong to Farmer Tebb. Bet he regrets that.”
 Use: MooMoo lore with a laugh.
Eldra Mosswhistle (Herbalist)
Location: Herbalist’s Hut (edge of town)
 One-liner:
“I won’t die for a flower, no matter how sick your mother is.”
 Use: Hard boundary that forces the PCs into the forest.
Mara (Seris’s Mother)
Location: Seris’s home
 One-liner:
“The moon flickers when I sleep… it wasn’t always like this.”
 Use: Emotional hook, quiet foreshadow.
Orrick the Lighthouse Keeper (Optional NPC)
Location: Abandoned Lighthouse
 One-liner:
“Something’s been calling from the fog. Sounds like grief.”
 Use: Atmospheric horror + sea mystery.
Tebb Hollowroot (Former Farmer)
Location: Outskirts / Market
 One-liner:
“Lost three cows. One came back wrong.”
 Use: Direct MooMoo setup without exposition.
Sister Alwen (Selûnite Acolyte — minor)
Location: Small Shrine to Selûne
 One-liner:
“The moon listens, even when it cannot answer.”
 Use: Subtle Selûne presence without revealing plot.
General Townsfolk
Location: Everywhere
 One-liner (rotate):
“Feels like the town’s holding its breath.”
 Use: Reinforce dread, scarcity, and isolation.
🌑 THE FAILED CURE & MARA’S LAST REQUEST (REVISED)
Scene Setting
Location: Seris’s home
 Tone: Intimate. Quiet. Heavy.
 Timing: Immediately after the party returns with the moonpetal
The party has done everything right.
 That’s what makes this hurt.
🌿 THE CURE ATTEMPT
Read-Aloud
The room is dim and warm with the scent of crushed herbs. Seris kneels beside her mother, fingers trembling as Eldra applies the poultice.
For a breath… it works.
Mara’s chest rises more steadily. Color returns to her cheeks.
Her eyes flutter open.
“Seris…”
Seris lets out a shaky breath she didn’t realize she was holding.
“I’m here. I’m here. You’re going to be okay.”
If the party casts healing magic now, allow it to help — but only to give Mara clarity, not life.
🌘 THE SHADOW REVEALS ITSELF
Read-Aloud
The lantern flame shrinks.
Not flickering — dimming.
A chill creeps across the floor, like cold water.
Dark veins surface faintly along Mara’s wrist, pulsing once… twice… then stilling.
Eldra recoils.
“No… that’s not sickness.”
If players investigate:
Medicine / Arcana / Religion:


 This illness is being sustained by something unnatural — something that does not want her to heal.
Healing magic now fails — not violently, just… refused.
🌙 MARA’S LAST LUCID MOMENTS
Mara inhales sharply.
Her eyes clear completely.
She knows.
She grips Seris’s wrist — harder than she should be able to.
“Listen to me.”
Seris shakes her head, tears spilling.
“Please don’t do this.”
Mara turns her gaze to the party.
She studies them — each of them.
MARA’S PLEA (READ THIS SLOWLY)
“I won’t be here much longer.”
Seris chokes.
“No—”
Mara silences her gently.
“You don’t see it yet. But you will.”
She looks back to the party.
“My daughter has never been alone… not until now.”
Her voice cracks.
“Please.”
“She doesn’t know the road ahead.”
“She doesn’t know who she is yet.”
Her grip tightens.
“Walk with her. Stand where I no longer can.”
This is the moment the players realize:
 this isn’t a request — it’s a charge.
🌒 THE WARNING
Mara’s gaze drifts toward the forest.
“Something there listens.”
“It wears the night like a cloak.”
She looks back, fear sharpening her voice.
“If you turn away… it will not.”
Mara’s breathing grows shallow. She shifts, mustering what little strength remains.
Her gaze fixes on the party — urgent now.
“Moonfall Grotto.”
The words are barely more than a whisper.
Seris stiffens.
“Mother…?”
Mara nods faintly.
“I felt it long before the sickness.”
Her fingers curl weakly into Seris’s sleeve.
“It calls… like the tide answers the moon.”
She looks back at the party.
“If there is anywhere the night hasn’t claimed yet… it is there.”
She swallows, struggling.
“Go to Moonfall Grotto.”
THE WARNING (TIGHT, CLEAR, OMINOUS)
Mara’s eyes glaze slightly — but her voice sharpens.
“You will hear bells.”
“You will feel watched.”
“Do not answer.”
Seris’s breath catches.
“What bells?”
Mara does not answer her.
She looks only at the party.
“The shadows will test you.”
“If you turn back, they will follow.”
This is the explicit instruction your players need.
THE FINAL CHARGE
Mara exhales slowly.
Her hand tightens once — just once — around Seris’s wrist.
“Please.”
“Do not let her walk that path alone.”
Her eyes meet the party’s one last time.
“Take her to Moonfall.”
Mara exhales slowly.
The shadows fade from her skin.
Her hand slips from Seris’s grasp.
For a heartbeat, nothing happens.
Then—
Seris makes a sound that isn’t a scream.
She presses her forehead to her mother’s chest, shaking.
“I brought it. I did everything you said. I brought it back.”
She repeats it, over and over.
“I brought it back.”
Let the moment breathe.
Do not rush this.
🕯️ AFTERMATH — SERIS’S BOND WITH THE PARTY
Later — that night or the following dawn — Seris approaches the party.
She looks different now. Older. Smaller.
She bows her head.
“My mother trusted you.”
She swallows.
“So I will too.”
She looks at them one by one.
“If you’re willing… I would walk with you to Moonfall Grotto.”
Her voice barely holds.
“Not because I’m brave.”
“Because I don’t know how to do this alone.”

documents.title: Moonfall Grotto
documents.content:
Level 1:
🌙 Moonfall Grotto – Level 0 (P0)
The Threshold of Moonfall
Purpose of This Level
Transition from the mortal world into the sacred
Establish Selûne’s presence without exposition
Give Seris a subtle emotional reaction
Signal that this place is not abandoned — merely waiting
Funnel the party toward P1A / P1B with tension, not urgency
This level should feel quiet, heavy, and intentional.
Arrival Description (Read Aloud)
The passage widens into a broad stone chamber, its floor laid with intricate patterns worn smooth by time.
 Moon motifs spiral across the walls, some cracked, some faded, but none defaced.
 At the chamber’s center stands a statue of Selûne — tall, serene, her gaze lifted upward.
 Two stairways descend from opposite sides of the room, disappearing into shadow below.
Allow silence after this description. Let players look around.
General Atmosphere
No hostile presence
Sound carries strangely (footsteps echo longer than expected)
The air feels cool, but not cold
Magic feels muted, but stable
This is not a dungeon yet.
 It is a threshold.
The Statue of Selûne (Central Feature)
Description
Weathered stone, not pristine
One hand raised toward the unseen sky
One hand open, palm outward
Base carved with moon phases
Passive Effect
Characters feel a sense of calm
Wounds ache less
Fear feels distant
No mechanical bonus — this is mood-setting.
Interaction: Touching or Praying
If a character:
Touches the statue
Offers a prayer
Speaks about loss, hope, or uncertainty
Describe one of the following (choose based on tone):
A faint silvery glow along the carvings
The sound of distant water
A momentary warmth in the chest
Nothing dramatic happens.
 This reinforces that Selûne’s influence is quiet, not theatrical.
Seris’s Reaction (Important)
Seris does not explain anything.
Instead:
She stops moving when she sees the statue
Her breathing steadies
If asked, she says:
“I don’t know why… but I feel like this place remembers something.”
Do not elaborate.
 This is emotional foreshadowing only.
Environmental Details & Interactions
Shadow Scars (Subtle Foreshadowing)
Thin, dark fractures trace parts of the walls and floor.
They are not spreading
They do not move
They feel wrong, but inert
Checks:
Investigation/Religion (DC 12): These appeared after the grotto was abandoned
Arcana (DC 15): This is not natural decay
No mention of Shar. Ever.
The Offering Basin
A shallow stone bowl near the statue.
Inside:
Old coins
Faded ribbons
Dried flowers
One recent offering, no more than a few years old
If a player adds something meaningful:
Make a note for later
No immediate reward
This will matter emotionally much later.
The Dried Moonwell
A circular depression carved into the floor.
Once held water
Now completely dry
Smooth stone, untouched for years
If players add water or light:
Moonlight briefly reflects
Then fades
This reinforces:
Selûne has not abandoned this place — but she is not intervening.
Flow Control (Very Important)
Players should feel free to:
Talk
Investigate
Reflect
Roleplay
But not linger indefinitely.
After ~10–15 minutes of table time, gently nudge:
From below, you hear faint sounds — movement, voices, or the crackle of fire.
This naturally leads them toward P1A or P1B.
Exits to Lower Levels
Stairway A – Pilgrims’ Way (P1A)
Slightly warmer air
Faint silver flecks in the stone
Feels welcoming, but sad
Stairway B – Watchers’ Descent (P1B)
Cooler
Narrower
Air smells faintly of smoke
Feels occupied
🌙 Moonfall Grotto — Side Altar Chamber (DM Guide)
Location Type: Selûnite Shrine Chamber
 Purpose: Optional trial, early reward, thematic foreshadowing
 Tone: Quiet reverence, balance, restraint
📍 ROOM OVERVIEW (FOR DM)
This chamber lies off the secondary staircase on the upper level of Moonfall Grotto.
Key Features:
A stone altar at the center of the room
Three sealed chests along the eastern wall
Faint moon motifs worked into the floor and altar
No enemies present unless the party behaves recklessly
This room is safe. It exists to reward curiosity, respect, and restraint.
🎭 READ ALOUD — ENTERING THE CHAMBER
The stone here is different — smoother, colder.
The air feels still, untouched by decay or shadow.
At the center of the chamber stands a low altar of pale stone, carved with crescent moons and flowing lines that curve toward one another without ever meeting.
Three chests rest against the far wall, sealed but untouched by dust, as if waiting.
Pause. Let them explore.
🌙 THE ALTAR — PRAYER INTERACTION
If a character examines the altar closely:
The carvings are deliberate and careful. This is not a place of power seized — it is a place of power granted.
Trigger Condition
The altar does nothing unless a character explicitly:
Kneels
Prays
Invokes Selûne
Or performs a respectful, intentional act of devotion
No spellcasting required.
✨ READ ALOUD — PRAYER SUCCESS
When a character prays:
As you place your hands upon the altar, the chamber grows subtly brighter — not with light, but with clarity.
The carvings along the altar warm beneath your touch.
Somewhere deep within the stone, something acknowledges you.
The three chests unlock with a soft click.
🎁 THE THREE CHESTS — WEAPON REWARDS
Each chest contains a Selûnite-blessed weapon. These are not artifacts, but meaningful early rewards.
Let the party decide who takes what.
🌙 Crescentblade (Sword)
A finely balanced sword etched with crescent patterns.
Effect
Once per turn, when you hit with this weapon, deal +1 radiant damage.
The blade reflects light even where none should reach.
🌙 Lunewood Staff (Staff)
A pale wooden staff, smooth as river stone.
Effect
When you deal damage with a spell cast using this staff as a focus, you may add +1 to one damage roll of that spell.
If used as a weapon, it deals +1 damage on a hit.
The staff feels warm in the hands, as though it remembers old prayers.
🌙 Moonstring Bow (Bow)
A bow with a silvery string that hums faintly when drawn.
Effect
Once per turn, when you hit with this weapon, you may either:
Deal +1 damage, or
Ignore half cover for that attack.
The bow seems to guide your aim rather than resist it.
🌓 RELIGION EASTER EGG — THE DIVIDED WHOLE
After the prayer and chest opening, call for this only once.
“If anyone is proficient in Religion, you may make a check.”
DC 13 Religion
✅ SUCCESS — READ ALOUD
As you step back from the altar, something subtle catches your attention.
The crescent moons carved into the stone are not identical.
Some curve inward.
 Others outward.
Together, they form a single design — not opposing symbols, but two halves of one continuous whole.
At the center, where the lines nearly meet, the stone is worn smooth…
As though something should be there — not missing, but divided.
Do not explain further unless asked.
OPTIONAL DEEPER INSIGHT (DC 17+ Religion)
This shrine was never meant to empower one alone.
It was built to honor balance — something once whole, now apart, yet bound by the same shape.
Stop there.
🌙 OPTIONAL SERIS MOMENT (STRONGLY RECOMMENDED)
If Seris is present:
Seris lingers at the altar longer than the rest of you.
“It feels… familiar,” she says quietly.
 “Not comforting. Just… known.”
She steps back, unsettled, and says no more.
This plants emotional weight without revealing anything.
🌙 MOONFALL GROTTO — ACT I COMPLETE DM GUIDE
P1B: Sharran Encounter (with detailed fight trigger)
P2B: Final Floor — Success Path
P2B: Final Floor — Failure → Rescue → Trial Path
The Trial of Selûne
The Artifact Choosing Seris
Revelation of the Other Artifacts
No matter the path, Act I always ends with the artifact binding to Seris and the world opening up.
🕯 P1B — THE SHARRAN ENCOUNTER
PURPOSE
Introduce organized opposition seeking the artifact
Establish Seris as a required key
Create a meaningful success/failure branch
Make the party protective of her
This encounter must occur.
ARRIVAL BLURB (READ ALOUD)
Low embers glow ahead. Bedrolls lie scattered against the stone.
One of the hooded figures looks up — then freezes.
Their gaze slides past you… and locks onto Seris.
SERIS’S IMMEDIATE REACTION
Seris (quiet, urgent):
“I don’t like this.”
A moment later:
“We should go. Now.”
SHARRAN ESCALATION — FIGHT TRIGGER FLOW
🔹 BEAT 1 — RECOGNITION (NO COMBAT)
The Sharrans do not attack immediately.
NPC lines:
Leader: “No… that’s not possible.”
Whispered: “She’s marked.”
Seris notices:
“They’re not looking at you. They’re looking at me.”
Sharrans subtly block exits. No weapons drawn.
🔹 BEAT 2 — DEMAND (LAST CHANCE)
The leader steps forward, palms open.
NPC lines:
Leader: “This doesn’t need to become violent.”
Leader (to Seris): “You’ll come with us. You’ll kneel. And we’ll all walk away.”
Intent becomes clear:
They want Seris alive
They believe she can make the shrine answer
If the party refuses, shields Seris, or tries to leave:
The leader exhales slowly.
 “Pity.”
🔥 BEAT 3 — COMBAT TRIGGER
Combat begins immediately if:
A weapon is drawn
A spell is cast
A Sharran reaches for Seris
The party attempts to flee with her
During combat, reinforce intent with callouts:
“Don’t damage her!”
“Break them — not her!”
“The shrine won’t answer us without her!”
OUTCOME BRANCH
✅ SUCCESS
Seris is protected
Sharrans retreat upward or flee
Proceed to P2B — Success Path
❌ FAILURE (SERIS DOWNED)
Combat immediately stops.
Sharran Leader:
“Now. Take her.”
As they retreat downward:
“Seal it. They won’t follow.”
A shadow barrier forms.
 The Sharrans believe the party cannot pass.
Proceed to P2B — Failure Path
🌙 DESCENT TOWARD P2B (ALL PATHS)
READ ALOUD
The stone smooths beneath your feet as you descend.
The air feels strained — like something below has been disturbed and rejected.
DM Notes
Selûne’s ambient favor allows traversal
The barrier weakens naturally over time
The Sharrans believe it is absolute — they are wrong
🌙 P2B — FINAL FLOOR (SUCCESS PATH)
(Seris was not captured)
ARRIVAL BLURB
The chamber opens wide beneath a fractured ceiling.
A pale lunar disc glows at the center of the floor.
The shrine stands untouched — patient, waiting.
SERIS IN THIS SPACE
Seris feels different here:
Calm
Focused
Drawn toward the shrine
Seris (quiet):
“I feel… clearer here.”
She can now fully heal the party between encounters without strain.
🌑 P2B — FINAL FLOOR (FAILURE PATH, BEFORE RESCUE)
(Seris was captured)
ARRIVAL BLURB
The light here flickers unevenly.
The shrine stands intact — but strained, like a breath held too long.
The shrine will not activate yet.
This signals clearly:
Someone who belongs here is missing.
WHAT HAPPENED (DM ONLY)
Sharrans brought Seris down
Tried to force her to pray
Failed
Retreated again in frustration
AFTER THE RESCUE
Seris (shaken):
“They kept asking me to pray. I told them I didn’t know how.”
Returning with Seris stabilizes the space.
 Proceed as the Success Path.
🌙 THE TRIAL OF SELÛNE (ALL PATHS)
TRIAL TRIGGER
The shrine responds only to willing prayer.
If the party hesitates, the shrine offers guidance:
“The moon does not yield to the untested.”
Encouraging Seris to pray grants subtle favor.
SENTINEL APPEARANCE (READ ALOUD)
The lunar disc brightens — then fractures with light.
A figure steps forward, blade already drawn, formed of silver and shadow.
Sentinel:
“Carry the light… and its burden.”
DURING THE TRIAL
The Sentinel does not taunt
It tests resolve and restraint
It never executes the fallen
Mid-trial line:
“Strength without purpose is hollow.”
END OF THE TRIAL
The figure kneels.
Moonlight pours back into the shrine.
Final words:
“The burden is chosen.”
🌙 THE ARTIFACT CHOOSES SERIS (READ ALOUD)
The moonlight does not fade.
Instead, it gathers — slowly, deliberately — toward Seris.
She freezes, breath caught in her chest.
Pause.
The light brushes her hands… and stops.
As if waiting.
If she accepts:
The glow tightens, anchoring itself to her like gravity finding its center.
Seris (whispered):
“I didn’t ask for this…”
WHAT THE PARTY FEELS
The shrine exhales.
The space feels settled — as though something inevitable has finally happened.
📜 THE LETTER UNLOCKS
Something stirs at her side.
The seal on the letter flakes away like dust.
Seris reads silently, then says:
“My father’s name… is Elyndor Vaeloris.”
 “He’s in Lunaryth.”
No more is revealed yet.
🌌 REVEAL OF THE OTHER ARTIFACTS
The shrine’s light fractures outward — not into one path, but many.
Reflections ripple across the stone: places of ruin, storm, silence, and frost.
Then, calmly:
“What was given once was never meant to stand alone.”
The party understands:
This artifact is one of many
Others exist across the world
Power is offered only to those who remain true to their ideals
If asked directly, the shrine responds:
“Conviction shapes the gift.”
“Power bends to belief.”
SERIS’S DEPARTURE — END OF ACT I
Seris:
“I need to understand this. And I don’t think I can do that with you watching.”
She asks the party to continue forward.
END STATE OF ACT I
Shadows recede
New paths open
Other artifacts await
The world expands

ENCOUNTER — QUIET WARDEN INTERVENTION
Location: Greyhaven shrine platform
 Party Level: 3
 Party Size: 3–6
 Expected Duration: 2–3 rounds
 Lethality: Low (control > damage)
WHEN THIS BATTLE STARTS
Combat begins only if:
The party continues shrine restoration after being warned
OR physically blocks the record-keepers
OR attempts to complete the name publicly
If the party stops restoring at any time → combat ends immediately.
ENEMY COMPOSITION
Default (Recommended)
3 Quiet Wardens
Scaling
Party of 3: 2 Wardens
Party of 5–6: 3 Wardens + 1 Warden Initiate (see below)
QUIET WARDEN
Medium humanoid (any), lawful neutral
 CR 1/2 (100 XP)
Armor Class 13 (padded coat, practiced movement)
 Hit Points 27 (5d8 + 5)
 Speed 30 ft.
STR 12 (+1)
 DEX 14 (+2)
 CON 12 (+1)
 INT 11 (+0)
 WIS 13 (+1)
 CHA 10 (+0)
Saving Throws DEX +4
 Skills Athletics +3, Insight +3, Perception +3
 Senses passive Perception 13
 Languages Common
 Challenge 1/2 (100 XP)
TRAITS
Measured Response
The Quiet Warden has disadvantage on attack rolls against creatures that are prone, restrained, or grappled.
(They are trained not to escalate.)
Nonlethal Doctrine
The Quiet Warden always deals nonlethal damage unless attacked with lethal intent after issuing a warning.
ACTIONS
Staff Strike
Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target
 Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage
Contain
Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target
 On hit, the target must succeed on a DC 12 Strength or Dexterity saving throw (target’s choice) or be grappled.
If the target is already grappled:
The target is restrained until the end of its next turn
Shove Aside (Recharge 5–6)
The Warden attempts to shove a creature within 5 ft.
Target makes a DC 12 STR save
On failure, pushed 10 ft. and knocked prone
REACTIONS
De-escalate
When a creature the Warden can see drops to 0 HP:
All Wardens immediately stop attacking
One uses their next action to stabilize the creature
This reinforces tone.
WARDEN INITIATE (OPTIONAL ADD)
Use only for 5–6 PCs
Medium humanoid, lawful neutral
 CR 1/4 (50 XP)
Armor Class 12
 Hit Points 16 (3d8 + 3)
 Speed 30 ft.
Action: Staff Strike (+3 to hit, 4 damage)
Trait:
 Hesitant — The initiate has disadvantage on its first attack roll each combat.
This NPC cracks under pressure easily.
TACTICS (VERY IMPORTANT)
Quiet Wardens:
Never focus-fire
Prioritize interrupting restoration
Use Contain over Staff Strike
Shove PCs away from the shrine, not toward danger
Do not pursue fleeing PCs
Never attack Eldrin or Lyra unless attacked first
They say things like:
“Please stop.”
“You don’t understand the harm this causes.”
“This doesn’t have to get worse.”
STOP CONDITIONS (THIS IS KEY)
Combat immediately ends if:
The party steps away from the shrine
The name is no longer being spoken
The stones are released
The Wardens do not:
Arrest the party
Confiscate gear
Seek revenge later
They simply resume the erasure process.
PLAYER VICTORY CONDITIONS
The party “wins” the encounter if:
They complete shrine restoration
OR force the Wardens to retreat
OR hold the platform for 3 full rounds
Victory does not require killing anyone.

 At initiative count 20 each round, PCs with Marsh Marks make a STR check or have movement speed halved.

THE WARDEN OF SHARED GRACE (REBALANCED)

 CR ~4 (solo, Tier 1–safe)
Armor Class 14 (natural armor)
 Hit Points 85 (10d10 + 30)

 DEX 10 (+0)

 WIS 14 (+2)

 Damage Resistances necrotic, poison
 Condition Immunities poisoned
 Senses darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 12
 Languages understands Common but cannot speak
EQUIPMENT
Tearstone of the Waning Tide (active)
While holding the Tearstone, the Warden:
Ignores natural difficult terrain
Has resistance to poison damage
Has advantage on saving throws against being frightened
TRAITS
Aura of Still Waters (5 ft.)
 Creatures of the Warden’s choice that start their turn in the aura must succeed on a DC 13 STR save or have their movement speed reduced by 10 ft. until the end of the turn.
Borrowed Relief (1/round)
 The first time a creature within 30 ft. regains hit points in a round, the Warden regains 3 hit points.
Cleansing Pulse (Reaction, 1/round)
 When the Warden fails a saving throw against a condition, it may choose to succeed instead.
ACTIONS
Slam
 Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target
 Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
 Target must succeed on a DC 13 STR save or be grappled (escape DC 13).
 If already grappled, the target is restrained instead.
RECHARGE (5–6)
Waning Pulse
 Each creature of the Warden’s choice within 15 ft. must make a DC 13 CON save.
Fail: 13 (3d8) necrotic damage
Success: Half damage
(No condition stripping — keeps Tier 1 safe.)
BRANCH ADD-ONS (USE ONLY ONE)
🔵 ELDRIN, RETURNED
Medium undead, neutral
Armor Class 12
 Hit Points 22
 Speed 30 ft.
ACTIONS
Measured Strike
 Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target
 Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage.
TRAITS
Persistent Form
 At the start of each round, Eldrin regains 5 HP while the Warden holds the Tearstone.
Unyielding Presence
 Eldrin has advantage on checks to maintain a grapple.
ROLE
Body-blocker
Grapple assistant
Emotional pressure
🔴 LYRA, WANING SHADE
Medium undead, neutral
Armor Class 13
 Hit Points 20
 Speed 30 ft., hover 10 ft.
ACTIONS
Waning Touch
 Melee Spell Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature
 Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) necrotic damage.
Twisted Benediction (Recharge 5–6)
 The Warden regains 10 HP, and Lyra takes 5 necrotic damage.
TRAITS
Dimming Radiance
 Creatures within 10 ft. of Lyra have disadvantage on the first saving throw they make against being frightened or restrained each round.
ROLE
Minor damage
Healer amplifier
Emotional disruption
🟢 NO NPC DIED — MARSH HUSKS
Use 2–3 weakened Marshbound Guardians:
15 HP
No Crushing Hold
Damage reduced to 4 per hit
They exist to:
Block
Be cleared quickly
Sell scale
HOW THE PARTY WINS
The fight ends when:
The Warden reaches 0 HP OR
The Tearstone is forcibly removed
 (Action, contested Athletics vs +6)
Once removed:
Warden loses Borrowed Relief & Cleansing Pulse
Warden takes 15 necrotic damage at start of each turn
Risen NPC collapses after 1 round
QUICK SAFETY LEVERS (MID-FIGHT)
Too Hard?
Remove Borrowed Relief
Reduce Warden HP to 70
Disable Waning Pulse
Too Easy?
Increase Aura radius to 10 ft.
Allow Borrowed Relief twice per round

documents.content:
ACT 2 ENDGAME — ENCOUNTER GUIDE (ECLIPSED VARIANT)
Elyndor, High Priest of Selûne — Bearer of the Eclipsed Vesperveil
Intended Party
3–6 PCs, Level 5
Seris present
One PC was previously attuned to the Crystal
This is the capstone fight of Act 2
Design Intent
Elyndor feels hard to pin down, not explosive
Crystal corruption = defense, reversal, inevitability
Fight rewards focus fire, positioning, and pressure
4–7 rounds depending on party size
CORE DIFFERENCE FROM BASE FIGHT
In this version:
Elyndor is much harder to disrupt
His damage is only slightly higher
The Crystal creates “oh shit” moments, not sustained dominance
The party must play around Lunar Reversal
ELYNDOR — ECLIPSED STAT BLOCK
Medium humanoid (elf), lawful neutral → fractured
AC: 17
16 base
+1 from Eclipse Ward
HP: 120
 (He needs the extra padding because players will focus him hard.)
Speed: 30 ft
Ability Scores
STR 10 (+0)
DEX 12 (+1)
CON 16 (+3)
INT 14 (+2)
WIS 18 (+4)
CHA 16 (+3)
Saving Throws
WIS +7
CHA +6
CON +6
Special:
Advantage on all saving throws vs spells & magical effects
 (from Eclipse Ward)
Resistances
Necrotic
Radiant (from Eclipsed Conduit)
PASSIVE TRAITS
Eclipse Ward (from Crystal)
+1 AC
Advantage on saves vs magic
 (Already baked into stat block)
Mantle of Authority (15 ft Aura)
Enemy creatures in the aura have disadvantage on the first saving throw they make each round
This aura does NOT break automatically in this version.
Eclipsed Conduit
Whenever Elyndor casts a spell of 1st level or higher:
He takes 3 necrotic damage (cannot be reduced)
This is very important for pacing:
Elyndor bleeds himself out if the fight drags
The party wins wars of attrition
ACTIONS
Multiattack
Elyndor either:
Casts one spell and makes one weapon attack, or
Casts two spells if neither deals damage
Moon-Touched Mace
Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit
 Hit:
1d6 + 2 bludgeoning (avg 5)
+1d8 radiant (avg 4)
Avg Damage: 9
Used when enemies get close or to finish weakened PCs.
SPELLCASTING
Spell Save DC: 15
 Spell Attack: +7
Elyndor casts as a 7th-level cleric equivalent.
At Will
Sacred Flame — 2d8 radiant (Dex save)
3/day each
Command (upcast to affect 2 targets)
Hold Person
Spiritual Weapon (2nd level, 1d8 + 4 force, bonus action)
1/day each
Spirit Guardians (3rd level, radiant)
Damage: 3d8 radiant (avg 13)
Use this early to control space
Silence
Use tactically against casters
REACTIONS
Lunar Reversal (1/day) (Crystal)
Trigger: Elyndor takes damage
 Effect:
Halve the triggering damage
Attacker takes 7 radiant damage
DM NOTE:
 Use this on:
A crit
A smite
A big spell
 Not on chip damage.
This should shock the table once.
BONUS ACTIONS
Shadow Mend (1/Encounter)
Elyndor heals 20 HP
Immediately takes 10 necrotic damage
Net +10 HP, but visually disturbing.
Spiritual Weapon
Standard rules
Attacks at +7, deals 1d8+4 force
SERIS — MECHANICAL ROLE (LOCK THIS IN)
Seris acts starting Round 2.
Special Guardian of Faith
Triggers once
Deals 20 radiant damage
Cannot be reduced or reversed by Lunar Reversal
This is intentional — Selûne rejects the corruption.
Afterward:
Seris uses healing (10–15 HP)
Or Sacred Flame (DC 14, avg 9 radiant)
She never out-DPRs the party.
PLAYER COUNTERPLAY (VERY IMPORTANT)
Disrupting the Crystal
Once per round, a PC adjacent to Elyndor may attempt:
STR or DEX Check — DC 14
On success:
Suppress Eclipse Ward until end of Elyndor’s next turn
Elyndor loses advantage on magical saves for 1 round
This is the martials’ big moment.
EXPECTED DAMAGE OUTPUT (ELYNDOR)
Expected Total DPR: ~25–35 depending on setup
 (High pressure, not bursty)
FIGHT DURATION & FEEL
Rounds: 5–7
Early fight: oppressive control
Mid fight: momentum swings
Late fight: Elyndor bleeding himself out
If the party plays smart, this ends cleanly.
END CONDITION
When Elyndor hits 0 HP:
Crystal immediately goes inert
Mantle of Authority ends
Radiant resistance ends
Seris’ decision happens after initiative ends.
ACT 2 ENDGAME — ALLIED FORCES
Elyndor never fights alone unless the party has achieved the Clean Fall perfectly.
There are two distinct allied configurations, tied directly to the end state.
🌓 END STATE I — CLEAN FALL
Truth Exposed, Authority Broken
Allies Present
👉 NONE
This is intentional.
Clerics step back
Guards hesitate
Guild witnesses murmur
Mechanically:
Elyndor has more HP
Crystal corruption is his only edge
Narratively:
He stands alone because no one believes him anymore
This version emphasizes:
Duel energy
Personal failure
Seris vs Elyndor
You already have this version correctly.
🌑 END STATE II — FRACTURED FALL
Truth Contested, City Divided
This is where allies come in.
ALLIED ENEMY PACKAGE — FRACTURED FALL
1️⃣ SELÛNITE JUSTICAR (x2)
Misled defenders, not villains
Role
Frontline pressure
Protect Elyndor early
Break formation once truth becomes undeniable
Stat Lite (Easy to Run)
AC: 16
 HP: 45
 Speed: 30 ft
Attack:
+6 to hit
1d8 + 3 radiant damage (avg 7)
Feature — Hesitation
If Seris is revealed or speaks directly:
Justicars have disadvantage on attack rolls for 1 round
Behavior
Start aggressive
Shift to defensive by mid-fight
Surrender or disengage if Elyndor drops below 25 HP
These are not zealots.
 They are soldiers following a trusted leader.
2️⃣ OPTIONAL — PALACE BATTLEMAGE (x1)
Adds chaos, not lethality
Use this if:
Party size is 5–6
You want more battlefield texture
Stat Lite
AC: 13
 HP: 38
 Speed: 30 ft
Spells
Magic Missile (3 darts, avg 10)
Hold Person (DC 14)
Shield (Reaction)
Behavior
Defensive
Panics if isolated
Will flee if Elyndor is clearly losing
HOW THEY FUNCTION WITH ECLIPSED ELYNDOR
Early Fight (Rounds 1–2)
Justicars form a loose line
Elyndor casts Spirit Guardians
Battlemage controls space if present
Mid Fight (Rounds 3–4)
Justicars begin to hesitate
Seris’s Guardian of Faith shakes morale
Crystal corruption becomes visible
Late Fight
Justicars disengage or surrender
Battlemage retreats or is ignored
Fight collapses back into Elyndor vs Party
This ensures:
Allies matter
But the climax is still personal
IMPORTANT BALANCE NOTES
If allies are present:
Elyndor’s HP is reduced to ~100
Crystal corruption stays the same
Mantle of Authority radius may be reduced to 10 ft if needed
This keeps total encounter difficulty stable.
WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT STRUCTURE
✔ Clean Fall = moral duel
✔ Fractured Fall = chaos and divided loyalty
✔ Allies reinforce Elyndor’s authority theme
✔ Seris’s presence directly affects the battlefield
✔ Fight devolves into isolation, which is perfect narratively
TL;DR (FOR AT-THE-TABLE USE)
Clean Fall: Elyndor alone, harder personally
Fractured Fall: Elyndor + 2 Justicars (+ optional Battlemage)
Allies peel away as truth becomes undeniable
Source | Avg DPR
Sacred Flame | 9
Spiritual Weapon | 8
Spirit Guardians (1–2 targets) | 13–26
Weapon Attack | 9

LEVEL 5 NPCs (TOP TIER)

AC 16 | HP 56 | Speed 30
