Round 1: Move → Attack twice
Mid-fight: Attack twice every turn
Finisher: Action Surge → 4 attacks in one turn
LETHALITY
If opponent drops to 0 HP, he keeps attacking unless physically stopped.
2) NYX AMBERLINE — Warlock 5 (Fiend) ⚠️ CONDITIONAL LETHAL Race: Tiefling
AC 14 | HP 48 | Speed 30
 CHA 18 | Spell DC 15 | Spell Slots 2 (3rd level)
ATTACKS
Eldritch Blast
2 beams, each 1d10 + 4 force
SPELLS (ONLY THESE)
Hex: Bonus action; +1d6 damage per hit (concentration)
Fear: Cone; frightened enemies drop weapons and flee
Fireball: 8d6 fire (use once max)
FEATURES
Dark One’s Blessing: Temp HP when she drops someone
HOW TO RUN HER
Claims Red only if safe
Opens with Hex
Eldritch Blast every turn
WHEN TO USE SPELLS
Fear: If enemy closes distance
Fireball: Only if opponent is tanky or crowd demands spectacle
TURN SCRIPT
Round 1: Hex → Eldritch Blast
Every turn: Eldritch Blast
Panic button: Fear
LETHALITY
Kills only if crowd is chanting for blood.
3) AMON THRICE-MARKED — Monk 5 (Open Hand)
Race: Human (Variant)
AC 16 | HP 50 | Speed 45
 Ki Points 5
ATTACKS
Unarmed Strike
1d8 + 4 bludgeoning
FEATURES
Multiattack: 2 attacks
Flurry of Blows (1 ki): +2 attacks
Stunning Strike (1 ki): CON save or stunned (no actions)
Step of the Wind (1 ki): Dash or Disengage as bonus
HOW TO RUN HIM
Claims Blue
Never stands still
WHEN TO USE ABILITIES
Stunning Strike: ONCE, when it can win the fight
Flurry: Only if stun lands
Step of the Wind: To escape bad positioning
TURN SCRIPT
Probe: Attack twice
Big turn: Stun → Flurry
If losing: Disengage and reset
4) SISTER HALWEN — Cleric 5 (Control) Race: Half-Elf
AC 16 | HP 52
 WIS 18 | Spell DC 15
 Slots: 1st×4 | 2nd×3 | 3rd×2
SPELLS (RUN ONLY THESE)
Spiritual Weapon: Bonus action attack every round
Guiding Bolt: 4d6 radiant, grants advantage
Hold Person: Paralyze humanoid
Healing Word: Bonus action heal
HOW TO RUN HER
Claims Blue
Lets weapon do the work
TURN SCRIPT
Round 1: Spiritual Weapon
Every round: Weapon attack + Guiding Bolt or Sacred Flame
Once per fight: Hold Person
Heal if <15 HP
LEVEL 4 NPCs (MAIN FIELD)
5) ERYND VALE — Fighter 4 (Tactician)
Race: Elf (High Elf)
AC 17 | HP 46
 Maneuvers 3 (d8)
ATTACKS
Longsword
1d8 + 3 slashing
MANEUVERS
Trip Attack: Knock prone
Precision Attack: Add d8 to hit
Disarming Attack: Drop weapon
TURN SCRIPT
Trip early
Precision when missing
Disarm flashy opponents
6) CAPTAIN ELRIC STONE — Paladin 4 (Honorable)
Race: Human
AC 18 | HP 50
 Slots: 3×1st | Lay on Hands: 10 HP
ATTACKS
Warhammer
1d8 + 4 bludgeoning
SPELL USAGE
Divine Smite: +2d8 radiant on hit
Heal: Lay on Hands if <15 HP
TURN SCRIPT
Attack every turn
Smite once to end fight
Never kills
7) KESS IRONSTEP — Barbarian 4
Race: Dwarf (Mountain Dwarf)
AC 14 | HP 48
FEATURES
Rage (1/match): Resistance +2 damage
ATTACK
Greataxe
1d12 + 4 slashing
TURN SCRIPT
Rage → Charge → Swing
Never disengages
8) MARRA VEX — Shield Fighter 4
Race: Human
AC 18 | HP 48
ATTACKS
Shield Bash: Knock prone
Shortsword: 1d6 + 3
TURN SCRIPT
Bash → Sword
Stick close
Blue sigil always
9) ROVAN GRELL — Ranger 4
Race: Half-Elf
AC 15 | HP 42
 Hunter’s Mark (1/match)
ATTACKS
Longbow
1d8 + 3 piercing (+1d6 from Mark)
TURN SCRIPT
Mark → Kite → Shoot
Disengage if cornered
10) TOMAS RHEEL — Bard 4
Race: Rock Gnome
AC 14 | HP 40
 Inspiration: 3×d6
SPELLS
Vicious Mockery: Default action
Hold Person: Once per fight
Healing Word: Emergency
REACTION
Cutting Words: Subtract d6 from hit/damage
TURN SCRIPT
Mockery every turn
Cutting Words on biggest hit
Hold Person for drama
11) VAELIN TRESS — Rogue 4
Race: Halfling (Lightfoot)
AC 15 | HP 38
 Sneak Attack: 2d6
ATTACK
Rapier
1d8 + 4 piercing
TURN SCRIPT
Attack → Disengage
Only stays close if enemy prone
12) ILYRA FEN — Wizard 4
Race: Elf (Wood Elf)
AC 13 (18 w/ Shield) | HP 36
 Slots: 1st×4 | 2nd×3
SPELLS
Mirror Image: Defensive setup
Scorching Ray: Main damage
Shield: Reaction +5 AC
Misty Step: Escape
TURN SCRIPT
Mirror Image early
Ray every turn
Misty Step if cornered
GUILD GAMES — ROUND 1 BRACKET (FINAL STRUCTURE)
🔥 FEATURE MATCHES
Level 4 NPCs vs Level 5 NPCs
(Crowd favorites, used to establish danger and tone)
These matches are not about balance — they are about teaching the table that the Games are real.
MATCH 1 — Discipline vs Brutality
Captain Elric Stone (Lv 4 Paladin)
 vs
 Tharos Blackvein (Lv 5 Fighter) ⚠️
Purpose
Introduces Tharos as a lethal threat
Shows mercy vs execution contrast immediately
Expected Outcome
Tharos wins
Elric is spared only if someone intervenes quickly
Crowd reaction: stunned silence → uneasy applause
MATCH 2 — Faith vs Control
Marra Vex (Lv 4 Shield Fighter)
 vs
 Sister Halwen (Lv 5 Cleric)
Purpose
Demonstrates sustain + control
Shows how fights can end without blood
Expected Outcome
Halwen wins
Marra yields after Hold Person / attrition
Crowd reaction: respectful, calm
MATCH 3 — Fury vs Speed
Kess Ironstep (Lv 4 Barbarian)
 vs
 Amon Thrice-Marked (Lv 5 Monk)
Purpose
Shows mobility vs raw power
Introduces Stunning Strike visually
Expected Outcome
Amon wins narrowly
Kess goes down swinging
Crowd reaction: roaring approval
MATCH 4 — Steel vs Shadow
Erynd Vale (Lv 4 Fighter)
 vs
 Nyx Amberline (Lv 5 Warlock) ⚠️ (conditional lethal)
Purpose
Shows magic vs martial mismatch
Introduces crowd-driven lethality
Expected Outcome
Nyx wins
Whether Erynd lives depends on crowd mood
Crowd reaction: divided, tense
⚔️ PLAYER MATCHES
Level 4 NPCs vs PCs
(Designed to be fair, readable, and fun)
Each PC fights one Level 4 NPC in Round 1.
You can assign these flexibly based on party composition, but here’s a recommended default mapping.
MATCH 5 — Control vs Precision
Vaelin Tress (Lv 4 Rogue)
 vs
 PC #1 (Martial / Frontliner)
Vaelin pokes and disengages
PC learns to manage spacing and sigils
Vaelin always yields at 0 HP
MATCH 6 — Song vs Steel
Tomas Rheel (Lv 4 Bard)
 vs
 PC #2 (Martial or Hybrid)
Tomas demonstrates denial, not damage
Great teaching fight for Cutting Words & Mockery
Tomas stabilizes the PC if he wins
MATCH 7 — Arrow vs Spell
Rovan Grell (Lv 4 Ranger)
 vs
 PC #3 (Caster or Mobile PC)
Clear Hunter’s Mark demonstration
Terrain and movement matter
Rovan retreats if badly hurt
MATCH 8 — Fire vs Nerves
Ilyra Fen (Lv 4 Wizard)
 vs
 PC #4 (Any)
Shows Mirror Image / Shield clearly
Fragile if pressured
Great “I get how wizards work now” fight
GUILD GAMES — STRUCTURAL UPDATE (DM GUIDE)
NEW TOURNAMENT RULES (PUBLIC vs REAL)
What the City Announces (Public Rule)
“The champion of the Guild Games shall be granted the prize and an audience beyond reproach.”
The crowd believes:
Winner gets everything
Everyone else gets glory or shame
What Actually Happens (DM Reality)
Top 4 finishers receive a formal invitation to the elite demonstration event
Only the final champion receives:
The material prize
Public recognition
Direct proximity to power (King + Elyndor)
This lets you:
Keep multiple PCs in play
Justify Elyndor observing more than one of them
Preserve stakes even if a PC doesn’t win outright
UPDATED THAROS BLACKVEIN RULE (CRITICAL)
This is excellent characterization. Lock it in as follows:
Tharos’s Personal Code
“Strength is proven by endurance.”
Mechanical Translation (For You Only):
If Tharos defeats an opponent while he is above 50% HP, he deems them unworthy and kills them
If Tharos is reduced to 50% HP or lower at any point in the fight:
He will not kill that opponent
He may still win, but he spares them
He considers them “worth remembering”
IMPORTANT: HP CHECK IS CONTINUOUS
It does not matter what HP he finishes the fight at
If at any point he drops to ≤50%, the opponent has proven worth
This gives you:
A hidden “mercy threshold”
A way for skilled or clever PCs to survive even if they lose
A terrifying incentive to actually hurt him
THAROS’S FIRST-ROUND SLAUGHTER (SCRIPTED)
You were clear: this happens.
First-Round Opponent
Use:
Captain Elric Stone (preferred, maximum emotional impact)
 OR
Any honorable, well-liked NPC
How to Run It
Tharos claims Red
He presses relentlessly
He wins without dropping below 50% HP
He executes the opponent immediately
Read-Aloud Moment (Use This)
Tharos does not hesitate.
The blade rises once — not in anger, not in triumph — simply because nothing stopped it.
The arena goes silent.
Crowd Reaction
No cheers
Delayed applause
Uneasy murmurs
Guards do not intervene
This sets the tone for the entire bracket.
UPDATED STAKES BY ROUND
Round of 16
Stakes: Reputation
Death: Rare (except Tharos’s match)
Purpose: Establish threats
Quarterfinals
Stakes: Invitation threshold becomes visible
Death: Possible
PCs start realizing top 4 matters
Semifinals
Stakes: Public legacy
Death: Very possible
Tharos becomes a looming presence
Finals
Stakes:
Winner: Prize + power
Loser: Survives only if worthy
Death: Absolutely possible
HOW TO HANDLE THE “TOP 4 INVITE”
When a PC Is Eliminated in Quarterfinals or Semis
They receive:
A sealed invitation
A public nod
Guild acknowledgment
You can phrase it as:
“Your name is recorded among those who stood.”
This keeps them relevant for:
The Vesperveil demonstration
Elyndor’s attention
Act 2’s climax
DM FAILSAFES (DO NOT IGNORE)
If a PC Loses Early
Engineer a narrow loss
Let them wound Tharos’s future opponent
Have a lethal NPC remove someone else
If a PC Faces Tharos Early (Unplanned)
Let them:
Drop him below 50% once
Be spared
Gain a terrifying reputation
This is better than winning.

documents.title: Circle of Promise
documents.content:
⚫ DM GUIDE — THE CIRCLE OF PROMISE
Optional Act II Encounter | The Weeping Marsh Approach
“Some places do not test worth.
 They test what you are willing to lose.”
LOCATION OVERVIEW
Name: The Circle of Promise
 Location: Forest clearing just before entering the Great Weeping Marsh
 Visible Features:
A circular stone clearing, roots forming a natural ring
A black stone obelisk at the center
Four glowing arcane circles spaced evenly around it
Each circle hums with a different colored sigil (red, blue, gold, green)
A rickety wooden stairway leads up into the clearing
The forest here is unnaturally still. Sound seems muted. The air smells faintly of iron and wet earth.
NPCS PRESENT
Eldrin Mossmere — Half-elf ranger, cautious, practical, survival-focused
Lyra Fenwillow — Human cartographer-scholar, curious, ambitious, stubborn
They have traveled with the party for several days and feel like allies by this point.
FIRST IMPRESSION (READ ALOUD)
The clearing opens suddenly, as if carved from the forest rather than grown.
At its center stands a tall, black obelisk etched with faint runes — old, deliberate, and sharp.
Four glowing circles surround it, each pulsing slowly, patiently.
Lyra steps forward, breath catching.
 “This… this wasn’t here on the maps.”
Eldrin grips his weapon tighter.
 “That’s because places like this don’t want to be found.”
THE OBELISK (DM ONLY)
This is a forgotten shrine of Bhaal, disguised as an arcane trial. It predates modern worship and was designed to extract sacrifice through choice.
The obelisk will activate if interacted with
The circles must be occupied for it to function
It does not reward wisdom or caution
It rewards survival through loss
The shrine is optional. Nothing forces the party to engage.
ACTIVATION MECHANICS
How It Works
One creature must touch or channel magic into the obelisk
Four others must stand on the glowing circles
Eldrin and Lyra may volunteer or be assigned
The Roll
The activating character makes a single d20 roll
DC 99
Only a natural 20 succeeds
Do not frame this as “impossible.”
 Let the players believe.
FAILURE PATH (DEFAULT OUTCOME)
Visual Sequence (READ ALOUD)
The obelisk pulses.
The circles ignite, one by one, light racing between them faster… and faster.
The glow becomes frantic — desperate — as if searching.
Then it stops.
One circle flares brighter than the rest.
Choose randomly between Eldrin and Lyra.
The stone beneath them fractures.
There is a single, sharp cry — then nothing.
The circle collapses inward, swallowing them whole.
AFTERMATH
The obelisk cracks violently and disintegrates
A ladder is revealed beneath it, descending into darkness
The forest goes silent
DESCENT SCENE
The ladder creaks under your weight.
The air below is cold, damp, and thick with the smell of blood.
Your light reaches the floor — and stops.
They find:
The NPC’s corpse brutally mauled
Bones broken, flesh torn
Signs of animal frenzy
Immediately trigger combat.
COMBAT: WOLF AMBUSH
4–6 Wolves (scaled to party size)
Easy for a full party
Overwhelming for one person
This fight is not the punishment — the death already was.
THE BROKEN REWARD
Among the remains lies a shattered weapon.
🗡️ Bloodbound Testament (Broken)
Mundane weapon
Cannot be attuned
No magical bonuses
You show the players the full, intact stat block anyway.
“You recognize the runes.
 You understand what this weapon was meant to become.”
Let them feel it.
SUCCESS PATH — NATURAL 20
Narration
The light freezes mid-pulse.
The circles glow together — steady, unified.
The obelisk cracks slowly, deliberately… and opens.
No one is taken.
REWARD (INTACT)
🗡️ Bloodbound Testament
Weapon (Martial), Requires Attunement
+1 to attack and damage rolls
+1d4 necrotic damage on hit
Once per long rest, when you reduce a creature to 0 HP, gain temp HP equal to your level
“The blade hums — but faintly. As if something expected was never claimed.”
The shrine collapses peacefully afterward.
NPC REACTIONS
IF ELDRIN MOSSMERE DIES
Lyra Fenwillow:
She doesn’t scream.
She stares at the body, hands shaking.
 “He told me not to touch it… I knew he was right.”
Becomes colder, reckless
Blames herself, not the party (outwardly)
Later seeks dangerous knowledge
May flirt with darker factions later in the story
IF LYRA FENWILLOW DIES
Eldrin Mossmere:
Eldrin kneels silently.
“Curiosity,” he mutters.
 “Always thinks it’s harmless.”
Blames the party openly
Withdraws or leaves after the encounter
May return later hardened or antagonistic
LONG-TERM CONSEQUENCES (DM ONLY)
This event reshapes party behavior
NPC grief persists across sessions
The broken weapon becomes a reminder
Later NPCs may recognize the shrine’s mark
Optional future line:
“Most people don’t walk away from places like that.”

documents.title: Lunaryth - State 2
documents.content:
STATE 2 — THE GUILD GAMES
Recruitment, Sponsorship, and Commitment
THE SCENE: THE FOUNTAIN BEFORE THE STADIUM
When to run this:
After the Red Light Passage reveal
When the party returns toward the Stadium / Guild District
Or the moment they agree they need legitimacy
READ ALOUD — SETTING
A broad fountain spills water in measured arcs before the stadium gates.
Six banners hang behind it, each bearing a distinct sigil.
The crowd here isn’t gathered in excitement — it’s gathered in expectation.
A well-dressed figure stands atop the fountain’s edge, voice carrying easily over the plaza.
THE RECRUITER’S PITCH (READ ALOUD)
“Lunaryth does not reward questions.”
“It rewards results.”
“The Guild Games are not chaos — they are clarity.”
“Each guild sponsors individuals, not armies. One fighter. One banner.”
“Sponsorship does not make you stronger.”
“It gives you one moment in the arena — a single edge that reflects who you fight for.”
“Use it well, and the city will remember your name.”
Pause. Let that land.
Then:
“Win, and you earn more than coin.”
“You earn standing.”
“And an invitation.”
Lower the voice slightly.
“A private exhibition.”
“A demonstration of the Vesperveil Crystal.”
“The King will be present.”
“As will the High Priest of Lunaryth.”
Do not name Elyndor.
PLAYER-FACING EXPLANATION OF GUILD BONUSES
The recruiter gestures to the banners.
“Each guild offers its champions one advantage — no more.”
“Not power. Not protection.”
“A moment.”
Then summarize (briefly, not mechanically yet):
Martial Concord — momentum and pressure
Artisan Compact — precision and correction
Scholar’s Consortium — foresight and defense
Mercantile League — spectacle and timing
Civic Wardens — discipline and survival
Lunar Synod — composure under pressure
“Choose what reflects you.”
“The arena will test it.”
(You can hand players a short written list here.)
HOW PLAYERS SIGN WITH A GUILD (THE PATHWAY)
This is intentionally simple, explicit, and irreversible.
STEP 1 — DECLARE INTENT
After the pitch, ask openly:
“Do any of you wish to register for the Guild Games?”
PCs may register individually
Not everyone has to compete
Seris does not register
NPC clarification:
“Spectators are welcome.”
 “Champions are recorded.”
STEP 2 — SPEAK TO A GUILD REPRESENTATIVE
Each banner has a visible recruiter nearby.
When a PC approaches a guild:
The recruiter asks one question
No dice yet — this is roleplay alignment
Example Prompts (Pick One per Guild)
Martial Concord:


 “When the fight turns ugly, do you finish it — or hesitate?”
Artisan Compact:


 “Would you rather win cleanly… or win certainly?”
Scholar’s Consortium:


 “Is victory worth blood if blood isn’t required?”
Mercantile League:


 “Would you rather be feared… or remembered?”
Civic Wardens:


 “If the rules fail you, do you still follow them?”
Lunar Synod:


 “When all eyes are on you — do you feel watched, or guided?”
No answer is “wrong.”
 This is about identity, not optimization.
STEP 3 — PROVISIONAL SPONSORSHIP
If the recruiter is satisfied (almost always):
“Very well.”
“You will fight under our banner.”
Mechanically:
The PC gains their Arena Bonus
They receive a Guild Mark (ribbon, sigil, token)
Their name is entered into the Games ledger
NPC line:
“From this point on, what you do reflects us.”
This is the moment commitment locks in.
STEP 4 — REGISTRATION COMPLETE (STATE 2 ENDS)
Once at least one PC is sponsored:
“Registration for this season’s Games is now closed.”
Use this read-aloud:
Ink dries. Seals are pressed.
Your names circulate — quietly at first.
Somewhere beyond the plaza, doors that were closed begin to loosen.
Lunaryth knows who you are now.
You have officially entered:
STATE 3 — THE GAMES BEGIN

documents.title: Lunaryth - Sharran Hideout
documents.content:
SHARRAN HIDEOUT — DM GUIDE (NON-COMBAT)
“What Was Allowed to Exist”
Purpose of This Location
This hideout exists to:
Make the later Elyndor confrontation earned
Show Shar as a symptom of neglect
Give the party knowledge with cost, not freebies
Reinforce Act 2’s theme: silence creates monsters
This is not a dungeon crawl.
 It is a contained narrative descent.
OVERALL TONE & PACING
Quiet
Maintained, not abandoned
No chanting, no ritual frenzy
Feels like a place that was meant to be temporary and never dismantled
If players ask “why hasn’t anyone stopped this?”
 That’s the correct question.
LOCATION FLOW (MAP-AGNOSTIC)
Use this as beats, not rooms.
Entry Passage — proof of recent use
Records & Storage — proof of permission
Shrine Chamber — proof of consequence
Inner Presence — proof that something stayed
BEAT 1 — ENTERING THE HIDEOUT
READ ALOUD
The stairway slopes downward at an awkward angle, stone giving way to brick that doesn’t quite match the architecture above.
The air smells faintly of incense and old metal.
This place isn’t abandoned — just quiet.
What the Party Notices
Recently oiled hinges
Sweep marks in the dust
Footprints going in, very few coming out
Important framing:
 This place is being maintained, not defended.
SERIS’ FIRST REACTION
Seris is alert here.
She says quietly:
“This wasn’t hidden because it was dangerous.
It was hidden because it was inconvenient.”
This line sets the emotional tone.
BEAT 2 — RECORDS & STORAGE
This is where the party earns information.
What’s Here
Crates of supplies (food, oil, parchment)
Maintenance logs
Sealed chests
Nothing is trapped.
 Nothing is locked unusually well.
That’s important.
THE RECORDS (VERY IMPORTANT)
Among mundane paperwork, the party finds:
1. Maintenance Logs
Regularly signed
Approved access routes
Dates extending back years
These are not forged.
 They are legitimate.
2. Intervention Requests
Requests to cleanse or dismantle the shrine
Stamped repeatedly:


 “No Disruption to Public Faith”
3. Selûnite Reliquary Ledger
Marked with the crest of Aelwyn Vaeloris
Two names scratched out
Annotation written later:


 “Not fit to be acknowledged.”
No signature — but the handwriting cadence matches Seris’ mother’s letter.
SERIS’ REACTION (KEY MOMENT)
When Seris sees this:
She doesn’t get angry
She doesn’t speak at first
She folds the page carefully and keeps it
If asked:
“I’ve seen this handwriting before.”
She does not explain yet.
This matters later.
BEAT 3 — THE SHRINE CHAMBER
READ ALOUD
The chamber opens into a low, circular room.
A small stone altar sits at its center, darkened by old blood and violet residue.
No candles burn. No prayers linger.
Whatever was done here… has already been done.
This is Shar without pageantry.
WHAT THIS SHRINE IS (IMPORTANT)
This shrine was:
Meant to observe Selûnite failures
Meant to record doubt
Never meant to grow
But it was never dismantled.
And that allowed something to accumulate.
INTERACTING WITH THE SHRINE
If a PC:
Touches the altar
Channels divine magic
Attempts to cleanse it
Describe:
A chill
Shadows pulling tighter
A sense of being watched, not attacked
This is your last warning beat.
Seris steps back instinctively.
She says:
“This isn’t worship.
It’s… what happens when no one answers.”
BEAT 4 — THE INNER PRESENCE (PRE-COMBAT)
This is where you foreshadow the Warden + Thrall without triggering combat yet.
READ ALOUD
The shadows along the far wall don’t retreat from the light.
They wait.
What Players Can Do
Draw weapons
Spread out
Speak
Attempt to leave
BEAT 4.5 — THE WARDEN STEPS FORWARD
“Someone Stayed”
This is the moment combat becomes unavoidable.
WHEN THIS TRIGGERS (ANY ONE)
Trigger this scene when one of the following happens:
A PC attempts to destroy, cleanse, or significantly damage the altar
A PC openly invokes Selûne by name in the shrine
A PC pockets or reads aloud from the Selûnite ledger
The party advances deeper toward the shadowed wall without retreating
You do not wait for all of these.
 Pick the first meaningful intrusion.
THE SCENE (READ ALOUD — SLOWLY)
The shadows along the far wall detach.
Not violently — deliberately.
A figure steps forward, armor darkened with age and residue, movements practiced and calm.
He does not raise his weapon.
“That’s far enough,” he says evenly.
“This place isn’t meant to be disturbed.”
This is the Sharran Warden.
THE WARDEN’S ROLE (IMPORTANT)
He is not here to:
Kill intruders
Protect Shar’s glory
Defend doctrine
He is here to:
Ensure nothing changes.
That distinction matters.
INITIAL DIALOGUE (BEFORE COMBAT)
Let the party speak.
The Warden answers calmly, professionally.
Example Lines (Use Sparingly)
If asked who he serves:
“I was told to stay.”
If asked by whom:
“The order didn’t matter. The silence did.”
If accused of heresy:
“No one cleans up what they don’t want to admit exists.”
These lines never name Elyndor — but they indict him.
SERIS’ REACTION (KEY)
Seris stiffens when she sees him.
She says quietly:
“You were never meant to be here this long.”
This is not fear.
 It’s recognition.
THE FINAL WARNING (LAST CHANCE)
After one exchange, the Warden says:
“If you leave now, nothing else has to happen.”
This is genuine.
If the party:
Retreats → combat does not happen yet
Hesitates → shadows deepen, pressure rises
Presses forward / refuses → combat begins
THE EXACT COMBAT TRIGGER
When the party commits:
Read Aloud:
The Warden exhales — slow, controlled.
“Then I’ll finish what I was told to start.”
He raises his weapon.
At the same moment:
The shadow behind him peels itself off the wall —
not summoned, not commanded —
simply released.
The Shadowbound Thrall emerges.
Roll initiative.
FINAL DISCOVERIES (BEFORE COMBAT)
Before initiative ever starts, the party can also find:
1. A Simple Bedroll
Someone lived here
Not a fanatic — a caretaker
2. A Personal Journal (Optional)
Short, restrained entries:
“They said no one would come.”
 “I was told to stay.”
 “I think it’s changing.”
This humanizes the Warden before the fight.

documents.title: Lunaryth - Endgame
documents.content:
ACT 2 FINALE — FULL DM GUIDE
“When Silence Stops Working”
SECTION 0 — DM ORIENTATION (READ ONCE)
NON-NEGOTIABLES
Act 2 ends in a massive battle
The party always leaves with the Vesperveil Crystal
Seris always confronts Elyndor
The city resolves into one of two end states
Shar is never chosen willingly — only reached through desperation
THE ONLY BRANCH THAT MATTERS
Did the party make the truth clear, or did they let ambiguity stand?
Everything else feeds that.
SECTION 1 — POST-GAMES NIGHT AT THE INN
Victory Without Relief
Location: Party’s inn
 Tone: Celebration that doesn’t quite land
 Purpose: Decompression + last influence on the ending
READ ALOUD
The inn is louder than it has been all week, but the sound doesn’t travel far.
Tankards clink. Laughter flares, then fades. Even the music seems hesitant — like it’s waiting for permission to be joyful.
Pause. Let the party roleplay freely.
FILLER NPCs (USE 2–3)
Arena Medic
“You fought clean. That’s rare.”
Guild Celebrant
“Top four get remembered. Winners get used.”
Selûnite Novice
“The moon watched today. I don’t think it liked what it saw.”
If pressed:
“Not angry. Just… quiet.”
SERIS HERE (IMPORTANT)
Seris:
Drinks sparingly
Watches reflections
Fingers the seal of her mother’s letter
If asked how she’s feeling:
“I just want tomorrow over.”
Insight:
She’s unsettled, not afraid
OPTIONAL — THE SHARRAN BASE (CONSEQUENTIAL, NOT REQUIRED)
THE HOOK
A restrained knock.
NPC: Junior Archivist
“I don’t think anyone’s planning anything.
I think no one’s been stopping it.”
They report:
Quiet movement under the museum
Altered records
Requests stamped “No Disruption to Public Faith”
IF THE PARTY GOES
They find:
A maintained Sharran altar (unused, not ritualistic)
Petitions ignored, not approved
A Selûnite reliquary ledger tied to Aelwyn Vaeloris
Two names removed
Annotation: “Not fit to be acknowledged”
Seris recognizes the handwriting cadence from her mother’s letter.
She says nothing.
 She keeps the document.
This pushes toward a Clean Fall later.
IF THEY DO NOT GO
Nothing happens now.
This absence will matter later.
SECTION 2 — MORNING SUMMONS
From Champions to Witnesses
Tone: Formal, final
“By order of His Majesty, your presence is requested.
The High Priest has personally endorsed the audience.”
If they visited the Sharran base, that line should feel wrong.
SECTION 3 — MOONSPIRE PALACE (OUTER HALL)
The Last Calm
READ ALOUD
Pale stone arches rise into moonlit glass.
 Footsteps soften here, as if the palace itself insists on reverence.
COURT FILLER NPCs
Senior Cleric
“Faith must appear unbroken.”
Noble
“Demonstrations are reassurance, not discovery.”
Palace Guard
“Once it starts, it doesn’t stop.”
THE KING
King Aldren
Earnest
Weary
Grateful
“You’ve given this city hope. I thank you.”
Insight:
He defers instinctively to Elyndor
INTRODUCING ELYNDOR
He is already present.
Describe:
Moon-white robes
Folded hands
Perfect composure
Behavior:
Watches the party
Brief glance at Seris
Looks away immediately
If spoken to:
“Faith survives because it is protected from disorder.”
PLAYER AGENCY PAUSE
Say clearly:
“You have a moment before the demonstration.”
Let them:
Speak privately
Observe
Make Insight checks
Do not resolve anything yet.
SECTION 4 — THE INNER SANCTUM
Faith as Performance
READ ALOUD
Moonlight pours through a crystalline aperture, striking the dais where the Vesperveil Crystal rests — suspended, flawless, expectant.
THE CRYSTAL CHOOSES
A PC resonates first.
Automatic attunement
Clean lunar glow
Confirms Selûne’s blessing (already held by the party)
Crowd reaction:
Relief
Awe
Hope
ELYNDOR ATTEMPTS CONTROL
He steps forward.
 He gestures.
 He speaks ritual words.
Nothing happens.
A pause.
Murmurs.
Authority cracks — but does not yet fall.
SECTION 5 — THE IGNITION
Seris’ Signal
This replaces all forced interruptions.
READ ALOUD
Seris shifts.
She doesn’t step forward. She doesn’t speak.
She simply meets your eyes — steady, searching — and gives a single, almost imperceptible nod.
This nod means:
“If you’re going to act, do it now.”
PLAYER INTERVENTION WINDOW (CRITICAL)
Pause completely.
Say:
“You have a moment.”
Players may:
Question Elyndor
Speak about truth, faith, or the Crystal
Present Shar-base evidence (if they have it)
Stay silent
Their tone and clarity determine the end state.
SECTION 6 — THE REVEAL
Truth Spoken Quietly
Elyndor responds defensively if challenged.
Use:
“No one is entitled to the truth if it endangers the city.”
This line is the tell.
SERIS STEPS FORWARD
She removes her disguise.
She does not accuse.
She asks:
“Was I a danger…
 or an inconvenience?”
Silence.
Elyndor does not deny it.
That silence is the reveal.
SECTION 7 — DESCENT INTO BATTLE
END STATE I — THE CLEAN FALL
Trigger:
 Clear exposure + decisive party action
What happens:
Clerics step back
Guards hesitate
The King looks to Elyndor
Elyndor realizes containment is impossible.
“Faith cannot be allowed to fracture in public.”
He draws on forbidden power openly.
Everyone knows who crossed the line.
END STATE II — THE FRACTURED FALL
Trigger:
 Ambiguity, hesitation, or contested narrative
What happens:
Accusations overlap
A defensive spell is cast
A guard panics
Chaos spreads
Elyndor draws power to survive.
No clear villain.
 Only collapse.
SECTION 8 — THE BATTLE
Order Versus Truth
Multi-phase
Elyndor empowered by desperation, not devotion
The PC with the Crystal stabilizes the field
Seris fights, but does not lead
SECTION 9 — SERIS’ CHOICE
Mercy or Blood
After Elyndor falls:
He says:
“If I had told the truth… the city would have burned.”
Silence.
Seris decides:
Mercy
Execution
This choice shapes Acts 3–4.
SECTION 10 — EPILOGUE
End of Act 2
Describe Lunaryth:
Stabilizing or fractured
Hopeful or tense
End with:
“The moon rises over Lunaryth… and does not look away.”

documents.title: Lunaryth - State 3 (Guild Games)
documents.content:
THE GUILD GAMES OF LUNARYTH
FULL DM GUIDE — ARENA, BRACKETS & EXECUTION
1. PURPOSE OF THE GAMES (FOR YOU, THE DM)
The Guild Games exist to:
Force the party into public visibility
Create controlled lethality after a safer Act 1
Introduce elite NPC threats
Funnel the party toward Elyndor and the Vesperveil Crystal
Let player moral choices be witnessed
Winning the tournament is not required.
 Being seen, tested, and remembered is.
2. THE ARENA (PHYSICAL SETUP)
Layout
Circular stone coliseum
Grass battlefield
Two large rock outcroppings (light cover, difficult terrain around)
No climbable walls
No exits once combat begins
Starting Positions
One combatant starts at the TOP
One combatant starts at the BOTTOM
Distance encourages:
Movement
Early positioning
Sigil play
Arena Tone
Loud
Public
Performative
Everyone is watching
3. ARENA SIGILS (MATCH-LONG — FINAL VERSION)
Two sigils are visible at match start.
GLOBAL RULES
Each sigil can be claimed once per match
Each combatant may claim only one sigil
Touching a sigil requires no action
Sigils deactivate immediately after being claimed
Effects last until the match ends
You should describe them as faintly glowing spiral marks embedded in the grass.
🔴 RED SIGIL — Mark of Relentless Momentum
Effect (Passive, Match-Long):
Once per round, when you hit with an attack (weapon or spell), you deal +1d6 damage.
Design Intent
Rewards aggression
Scales naturally over the fight
Pressures defensive opponents
NPC Use
Aggressive fighters prioritize this
Tharos always takes this if able
🔵 BLUE SIGIL — Veil of Measured Defense
Effect (Passive, Match-Long):
Once per round, when you are hit by an attack, reduce the damage by 1d6.
Design Intent
Smooths burst damage
Increases survivability
Rewards patience and spacing
NPC Use
Defensive or tactical fighters prefer this
Casters and duelists often bait Red, then take Blue
ANNOUNCER CALLOUTS
“They’ve taken the mark — that choice will shape the rest of this fight!”
“Again! The sigil pays off!”
“They weather the blow — disciplined control!”
4. MATCH FLOW (HOW TO RUN EACH FIGHT)
Step-by-Step
Announce Fighters
Place Minis (Top & Bottom)
Describe Sigils
Ring the Bell
Run Combat Normally
Victory Conditions
Match ends when a combatant:
Drops to 0 HP
Submits
Is clearly incapacitated
Killing
Allowed
Socially charged
Always pause before a killing blow
“You have them. The crowd holds its breath.
 What do you do?”
5. ANNOUNCER & CROWD PERFORMANCE
Announcer Personality
Loud
Slightly biased toward drama
Not omniscient
Loves momentum shifts
SCRIPT TEMPLATES
Opening:
“LUNARYTH!
 The Guild Games begin — where steel decides what words cannot!”
Sigil Claimed:
“A bold choice — that mark will follow them to the end!”
Low HP Moment:
“They’re fading! This is the moment!”
Mercy Shown:
“Mercy… Lunaryth will remember.”
Kill:
(Silence)
 “…So be it.”
CROWD STATES (USE LIBERALLY)
Excited — cheers, chants
Uneasy — murmurs
Hostile — boos
Reverent — silence
Crowd tone can justify:
Healers hesitating
Guards intervening
Political consequences
6. TOURNAMENT STRUCTURE (16-FIGHTER BRACKET)
Composition
Total fighters: 16
PCs: however many register
NPCs: fill remaining slots (you’ve designed 12)
Seeding Rules
PCs placed as far apart as possible
No PC vs PC until late rounds
Lethal NPCs seeded away from each other
Rounds
Round of 16
Quarterfinals
Semifinals
Finals
You only fully run:
PC fights
Key NPC fights that foreshadow danger
7. NPC VS NPC MATCHES (FAST RESOLUTION)
Do not run these blow-by-blow.
Resolution Method
Decide narrative winner
Roll 1d6:
1–2: Clean win
3–4: Hard-fought
5: Upset
6: Controversial finish
Describe cinematically
Fully Play an NPC Match ONLY IF:
A PC is scouting the opponent
It involves Tharos or Nyx
It directly affects bracket tension
8. LETHAL NPCS (SPECIAL RULES)
Tharos Blackvein
Always tries to kill
Takes Red Sigil
Never grandstands
Crowd reaction: fearful respect
Nyx Amberline
Plays to the crowd
Kills if encouraged
Enjoys sigil play
Use them to teach stakes, not punish players.
9. DIFFICULTY & FAILSAFES (CRITICAL)
Survival Expectations
Level 5 PC vs Tharos:
~70–85% survival
~55–65% win chance
Hard Rules You Should Follow
Early matches = Level 4 NPCs
At least one PC reaches semifinals
You may justify advancement via:
Withdrawals
Injuries
Political interference
Crowd reaction
Never let the story stall because of dice.
10. WHAT THIS ARC ACHIEVES
By the end of the Games:
The party is known
Guilds have opinions
Elyndor has noticed them
Seris has a public path forward
Act 2 is ready to climax

documents.title: Greyhaven
documents.content:
SIDE QUEST DM GUIDE
THE NAME THEY STOPPED SAYING
(Aelwyn Vaeloris)
Placement:
 On the road to the Weeping Marsh, before the Circle of Promise
NPCs Present:
 Eldrin Mossmere, Lyra Fenwillow
Town Type:
 Small crossroads town directly adjacent to the dismantled shrine platform
Primary Themes:
 Erasure through mercy · Memory as danger · Control without cruelty
PURPOSE OF THIS ENCOUNTER
Provide a clear, urgent call to action
Introduce Aelwyn Vaeloris before Lunaryth
Show Sharran influence operating through civic process
Give Eldrin & Lyra a lived emotional response
Make shrine restoration feel like intervention, not curiosity
THE TRUTH (DM-ONLY)
The shrine honored Aelwyn Vaeloris, ancient heroine and matriarch of the Vaeloris line
It was dismantled via civic order, not vandalism
The process was guided by a Sharran influence cell (the Veilward Compact)
Forgetting is actively enforced, not passive
The erasure is ongoing — not complete yet
The party arrives mid-process, not after the fact.
ARRIVAL — READ ALOUD
The road opens into a compact settlement gathered around a crossroads.
Low stone buildings, clean paths, and a single raised platform sit just beyond the town’s edge — close enough that it’s impossible not to notice.
Whatever once stood there is gone.
The space around it feels… managed.
People don’t linger near it.
They walk around it.
The town and shrine platform are visible at the same time.
THE TOWN AT A GLANCE
One inn
A small square
The dismantled shrine platform
No guards
No fences
No obvious tension
Everything appears orderly.
KEY LOCATION — THE INN
The Stillwater Hearth
Warm, clean, quietly full.
This is where the call to action begins.
NPC CAST (ACTABLE)
Mirela Thorne — Innkeeper
Controlled kindness, civic loyalty
Mid-40s, composed, efficient
Believes she is protecting the town
Opening Line
“Travelers are always welcome. Supper’s on soon.”
If asked about the platform:
“That was… retired.
 It caused problems.”
If pressed:
“People don’t need symbols that make them argue.”
Tomas Renn — Server / Stablehand
Young, frightened, remembers
Early 20s
Knows more than he should
Afraid of saying the wrong thing
If spoken to quietly:
“They said I could lose my work if I kept asking.”
If asked what he was asking:
“Why we stopped leaving flowers.”
Old Jessa — Long-Term Guest
Waiting, not hiding
Elderly, calm, lucid
Has outlasted the process
Opening line:
“You can still feel her there, can’t you?”
If asked who:
“That’s the part they’re finishing tonight.”
THE STRONG CALL TO ACTION
THE INCITING EVENT
During dinner at the inn:
A group of town record-keepers (not guards) enters carrying:
A ledger
Blank stone plaques
Wrappings for removed offerings
They sit at a corner table near the window facing the shrine platform.
Read Aloud
One of them opens a ledger and begins reading quietly.
Another unrolls a blank plaque and checks its measurements.
Outside, you see someone begin clearing the last remaining offerings from the platform.
This is not rumor.
 This is the final step.
NPC REACTION (CRITICAL)
Tomas freezes.
Old Jessa stands immediately.
“No.
 You said you’d wait until winter.”
Mirela (tight, controlled):
“Jessa, please.
 This is the safest way.”
WHAT THE RECORD-KEEPERS SAY (CALM, DAMNING)
If confronted:
“We’re completing the record.
 Once this is logged, there won’t be confusion anymore.”
If asked what happens if they don’t:
“People keep remembering different versions.
 That causes harm.”
This makes it clear:
If the party does nothing, the shrine will be erased permanently tonight.
That’s the call to action.
NPC COMMENTARY (USE ONE EACH)
Eldrin
“This isn’t history being forgotten.
 This is history being finalized.”
Lyra
“If they finish this, no one will even know what they lost.”
INVESTIGATING THE SHRINE (IMMEDIATE OPTION)
Read Aloud
Up close, the stone platform is immaculate.
Tool marks show careful dismantling.
No stone broken.
 No offering crushed.
Someone wanted this to look merciful.
Visible with inspection:
Feminine outline
Motion in the pose
Partial engraving:
Va-l-r-s
No roll required.
MOVING TO RESTORATION (TIME PRESSURE)
If the party hesitates:
Offerings are removed one by one
The blank plaque is prepared
The ledger entry is nearly complete
Old Jessa
“If they write it down like that, it’s gone for good.”
This is now or never.
RESTORATION PROCESS (INTERRUPTING ERASURE)
Restoration is active resistance, not rebuilding art.
Steps:
Physically re-stack stones
Clean remaining etchings
Speak Va-l-r-s aloud in the open
Place a personal offering
As soon as step 3 happens:
The record-keepers stand
The process escalates
INTERVENTION — QUIET WARDENS
Arrival (Read Aloud)
Footsteps approach — unhurried, deliberate.
Three figures position themselves between you and the platform.
One closes the ledger.
“This is your warning.
 If you finish this, we intervene.”
They believe they are preventing harm.
IF COMBAT OCCURS (OPTIONAL)
Short (2–3 rounds)
Focus on restraint, interruption, shoves
Ends immediately if restoration stops
No pursuit
They are enforcing policy, not seeking blood.
RESOLUTION OUTCOMES
🟢 FULL RESTORATION
Shrine stands again (imperfect)
Name remains fragmented
Record-keepers withdraw silently
The ledger entry is never completed
🟡 PARTIAL RESTORATION
Shrine stabilized but unnamed
The name preserved privately
Erasure halted, but not reversed
🔵 PRIVATE PRESERVATION
No physical restoration
The ledger is completed
Only the party carries the name
Each path matters later.
EXIT LINE (FINAL — READ ALOUD)
As the party departs toward the Circle of Promise:
Old Jessa
“They still keep her likeness in the city.
They just stopped telling the story that went with it.”

documents.title: Lunaryth - State 1
documents.content:
LUNARYTH — STATE 1 DM GUIDE
“To Be Seen”
STATE IDENTITY (DM ONLY)
Seris has been found at the statue of Aelwyn Vaeloris
The party has learned from the letter:
Seris’ father is alive
He lives in Lunaryth
He is powerful, protected, and unreachable through normal means
The city is no longer indifferent
Elyndor is not named
The party is being observed, evaluated, and quietly discussed
Theme:
In Lunaryth, access is not taken — it is granted.
DESIGN INTENT
State 1 exists to accomplish three things:
Make it clear the party cannot reach the elite quietly
Present one legitimate path forward (the Guild Games)
Build pressure without forcing immediate action
Players should leave State 1 thinking:
“We won’t get anywhere unless we make ourselves known — publicly.”
GLOBAL STATE 1 BEHAVIOR (APPLIES EVERYWHERE)
Layer these cues into all interactions:
NPCs pause before answering Seris
Conversations lower in volume around her
Names of elites are avoided
Guards observe but do not interfere
Clerics are formal, restrained, procedural
Reusable NPC phrases:
“That’s not discussed openly.”
“You should be careful where you ask that.”
“Those matters require standing.”
THE LETTER (STATE 1 VERSION)
If not already read, introduce it shortly after the statue interaction or when players ask what Seris knows.
READ ALOUD
Seris,
If you are reading this, then I am gone — and you have lived.
Your father did not die as you were told.
He lives in Lunaryth.
He is a man of stature, shielded by title and reverence.
I cannot name him without endangering you.
If you seek him, do so carefully. Ask questions only where truth is already unwelcome.
Trust what pulls at you.
— Your mother
Seris’ Response (Anchor Line)
“If he’s this protected…
 then I was never meant to find him.”
LOCATION-BY-LOCATION — STATE 1
Each location mirrors the same structure so you can reference quickly.
🏛️ CENTRAL SQUARE & STATUE OF AELWYN VAELORIS
Atmosphere
Quieter than expected
People linger at a distance
The statue feels watched, not revered
Description (Read Aloud)
The statue rises from the square — a woman in pale stone, armored, composed, uncelebratory.
At the base, a plaque reads:
Aelwyn Vaeloris
 Champion of the Lunar Age
 Bearer of the First Light
No one comments on the name.
NPC: Temple Attendant (Measured, Neutral)
“Most people don’t linger here.”
“The statue represents unity. Not history.”
If asked about lineage:
“Lineage invites questions. Lunaryth prefers answers.”
Purpose of This Location
Establishes legacy
Reinforces that history is controlled
Makes Seris’ pull feel meaningful but unexplained
🍺 THE INN DISTRICT
Atmosphere
Still welcoming
Noticeably quieter when Seris enters
Advice replaces gossip
NPC: Innkeeper (Quiet, Firm)
“You’re welcome here.”
“But people like you don’t disappear into Lunaryth.”
“You either get ignored… or you get noticed.”
If asked how to be noticed:
“Win something.”
NPC: Bera Holt, Merchant (Directional)
“If you’re asking questions, you won’t get far on names alone.”
“Power listens to results.”
Purpose of This Location
First explicit suggestion that status precedes access
Soft introduction of competition as legitimacy
🧭 MARKET STREETS & CIVIC OFFICES
Atmosphere
Procedural
Careful
Records over people
NPC: Eldeth Varrow, Archivist’s Assistant
“Lineage records don’t open to strangers.”
“They open to names people recognize.”
If pressed:
“Right now, yours doesn’t circulate.”
Purpose of This Location
Confirms bureaucracy enforces invisibility
Reinforces need for public standing
🔻 RED LIGHT PASSAGE
Atmosphere
Less guarded
More honest
Truth closer to the surface
Recognition Scene (If Seris Is Present)
The older woman’s gaze lingers on Seris just a moment too long.
“No…”
“You were supposed to be dead.”
NPC: Maela Greythread
“Your mother worked here.”
“Someone powerful made sure she was forgotten.”
“If you want truth, girl — you won’t find it above ground.”
Purpose of This Location
Emotional validation for Seris
Confirms power acted deliberately
Pushes the party away from secrecy and toward confrontation by system
🏟️ STADIUM & GUILD DISTRICT
PRIMARY CALL TO ACTION
Atmosphere
Structured
Competitive
Evaluative
NPC: Kael Rennic, Retired Duelist (Explicit)
“You want access to the people who matter?”
“Then stop asking.”
“Guilds watch the Games.”
“The Council watches the guilds.”
“And the king listens to whoever the Council can’t ignore.”
This is the clearest call to action in State 1.
What Players Learn Here (Explicitly)
Outsiders cannot approach elites quietly
Guild sponsorship is the accepted path
The Guild Games are upcoming
Winners earn legitimacy, not just coin
What Is Still Blocked
Registration (State 2)
Official matches
Favor tracking
Purpose of This Location
Hardens the funnel
Makes the next step obvious without forcing it
Turns the spotlight into a choice
🏛️ THE MUSEUM
Atmosphere
Polite tension
Subtle restriction
NPC: Junior Curator
“Certain exhibits are under internal review.”
“I’m afraid that includes family histories.”
Purpose of This Location
Reinforces information lockdown
Prepares for later Sharran discovery
Confirms elites are already reacting
🏛️ TEMPLE DISTRICT (SURFACE LEVEL)
Atmosphere
Formal
Emotionally distant
Ritual without warmth
NPC: Junior Acolyte Lysa
“I used to feel something when I prayed.”
“Now it just… echoes.”
Do not expand yet.
WHAT STATE 1 PREVENTS (IMPORTANT)
Do not allow:
Naming Elyndor
Audience with the king
Discovery of the Sharran base
Access to the Vesperveil Crystal
Participation in the Games
If players push:
They are redirected to legitimacy, not blocked.
STATE 1 END CONDITION (DM ONLY)
State 1 ends when the party accepts visibility by doing any one of the following:
Deciding to participate in the Guild Games
Seeking a guild sponsor
Publicly declaring intent to compete
At that moment, the city shifts into:
STATE 2 — Registration & Sponsorship
No cutscene.
 Paperwork, ceremony, and attention begin.

documents.title: Lunaryth - State 0
documents.content:
LUNARYTH — STATE 0 DM GUIDE
“The City That Works”
STATE SUMMARY (DM ONLY)
The party has arrived in Lunaryth from the Weeping Marsh
They know an artifact exists somewhere in the city, but not where
Seris has arrived independently and has not yet been encountered
Elyndor is unaware of the party
Selune’s absence is not yet noticeable
The city is calm, prosperous, and confident
Theme:
Order without cruelty. Truth without urgency. History without detail.
DESIGN INTENT (FOR YOU)
State 0 exists to:
Establish normalcy
Teach players how Lunaryth functions
Prevent early access to deep truths without hard locks
Let curiosity build naturally
Make the State 1 transition feel inevitable
Players should feel:
“We can go anywhere… but nothing is quite opening yet.”
ARRIVAL SCENE — READ ALOUD
Pale stone walls rise ahead, unmarred and clean, banners drifting lazily in the wind.
Lunaryth does not feel fortified — it feels finished.
Guards at the gate wave travelers through with practiced ease. Merchants call out prices. Bells ring the hour somewhere within the city — not as warning, but as reassurance.
Whatever troubles exist beyond these walls, they do not seem to live here.
LOCATION-BY-LOCATION: STATE 0
Each location below includes:
What players can do
What they learn
What is prevented
NPCs you can immediately act out
🏛️ CENTRAL SQUARE & STATUE OF AELWYN VAELORIS
(Before Seris is encountered)
Description
Large statue of a woman in armor
Calm, composed stance
No religious iconography
Plaque reads: Aelwyn Va-l-r-s
Treated as civic art, not a shrine
What Players Can Do
Observe the statue
Ask who Aelwyn was
Walk the square
Visit surrounding buildings
What They Learn (Sanitized)
Aelwyn was a founding hero
Her era was “turbulent”
Her legacy is “symbolic”
NPCs Here
Calven Duskward — Civic Guide
 Polished, proud, shallow knowledge
“Founders are symbols. Symbols keep people together.”
“Details change. Meaning doesn’t.”
Hard Limits (STATE 0)
No lineage discussion
No emotional responses
No recognition of Seris
No divine framing
DM Note:
 The statue should feel important but inert.
🍺 THE INN DISTRICT
Tone
Warm, social, complacent.
What Players Learn
The king is distant but beloved
The High Council manages spiritual affairs
Guilds are the real gatekeepers
Outsiders don’t get royal audiences casually
NPCs
Innkeeper (choose name freely)
 Genuinely proud of Lunaryth
“If there’s trouble elsewhere, it hasn’t reached us.”
“That’s the benefit of order.”
Bera Holt — Traveling Merchant
 Knows roads, not politics
“Trouble doesn’t travel uphill to Lunaryth.
 It rolls off.”
What They Cannot Learn
Anything critical of Elyndor
Anything about Selune’s silence
Anything about Shar
Anything about Seris
🧭 MARKET STREETS / CIVIC OFFICES
What Players Can Do
Ask about records
Ask about the king
Ask about history
NPC
Eldeth Varrow — Archivist’s Assistant
 Tired, careful
“If it’s not in the record, it didn’t happen.”
“If it’s revised… it happened differently.”
Hard Limits
No archive access
No lineage records
No sealed documents
Redirect with:
“That requires formal request.”
🧭 CITY GUARDS & OFFICIALS
Behavior
Polite
Efficient
Uncurious
Sample Dialogue
“Royal audiences require sponsorship.”
“The guilds handle external petitions.”
“Lunaryth values stability.”
Never escalate guards in State 0.
 They are not antagonists — they are procedure.
🔻 RED LIGHT PASSAGE (STATE 0)
Tone
Dim, ignored, tolerated.
What Players Can Do
Enter
Observe
Talk casually
What Cannot Happen Yet
No recognition of Seris
No mention of her mother
No accusations
No emotional reveals
NPC
Maela Greythread (Dormant)
 Observant, reserved
STATE 0:
“You’re not from here.”
 “That’s not an insult.”
This NPC wakes up in State 1.
🏟️ THE STADIUM (OBSERVATION ONLY)
What Players See
Training bouts
Guild banners
Ritualized combat
NPC
Kael Rennic — Retired Duelist
 Bitter but honest
“The fights are clean.
 The favors aren’t.”
Hard Limit
No registration
No competition
No favor earned
Reason:
“Guild sponsorship required.”
🏛️ TEMPLE DISTRICT (SURFACE ONLY)
Tone
Formal. Distant. Bureaucratic faith.
NPC
Junior Acolyte Lysa
 Nervous, sincere
“Sometimes the prayers feel… echoed.”
 “Like they don’t go anywhere.”
Do not linger here yet.
WHAT IS COMPLETELY UNAVAILABLE IN STATE 0
Do not allow:
The Sharran base
The underground altar
The Vesperveil Crystal
Any criticism of Elyndor
Any divine conflict
Any reference to Seris’ mother or brother
Use:
Procedure
Politeness
Normalcy
Never:
Threats
Stonewalling
“You can’t do that”
STATE CHANGE EVENT
SERIS AT THE STATUE
This is the only event that transitions State 0 → State 1.
Trigger it when:
Players revisit the square
Curiosity peaks
Pacing feels right
READ ALOUD — STATE TRANSITION SCENE
The square is quieter now.
A lone figure stands at the base of the statue.
Seris.
She hasn’t noticed you yet. Her hand rests against the stone, fingers pressed flat as though she expects it to answer her.
Her expression isn’t grief or fear — it’s recognition without memory.
Something here has found her.
Pause. Let players act.
SERIS’ FIRST WORDS
“I don’t know why I came here.”
“But I couldn’t not.”
THE LETTER — CONTROLLED REVEAL
When asked why she came, Seris produces the letter.
READ ALOUD — LETTER CONTENT
Seris,
If you are reading this, then I am gone — and you have lived.
Your father did not die as you were told.
He lives in Lunaryth.
He is a man of stature, shielded by title and reverence.
I cannot name him without endangering you.

documents.title: The Weeping Marsh
documents.content:
ACT II — THE WEEPING MARSH
FULL DM GUIDE (Narrative, Systems, Dialogue)
CAMPAIGN ROLE
The Weeping Marsh is the first true Act II location.
Its job is to:
Force the party to act before reaching Lunaryth
Introduce the idea that comfort can be dangerous
Make death and mercy mechanically meaningful
Assign and bind the second artifact to the party
Create asymmetric fallout between Eldrin and Lyra
Player takeaway:
“Nothing attacked us — and that was worse.”
CORE THEMES (DM-ONLY)
The land reacts; it does not hunt
Preservation without release becomes corruption
Consequences are delayed, not immediate
The artifact is the problem — not the marsh
Never explain these outright.
GLOBAL SYSTEMS
Marsh Perception
All Perception checks in the Weeping Marsh are made at disadvantage
Environmental, not magical
Do not justify unless asked
Marsh Marks (Hidden Tracking)
When a PC:
Fails a Perception check and
Fails the associated saving throw
→ Assign 1 Marsh Mark (track secretly).
Marsh Marks do nothing immediately
They activate during the Well Guardian battle
Represent the marsh learning how the party moves
You only need 1–3 total Marks to matter.
ARRIVAL AT THE MARSH
Read Aloud — First Impression
The trees ahead bend inward, their branches woven so tightly that moonlight barely reaches the ground.
The water is shallow, dark, and still — not stagnant, but watchful.
Sound doesn’t echo here. It simply… stops.
Every step feels like it’s being remembered.
NPCs react quietly. Let silence do work.
Eldrin — First Reaction (Optional)
“This isn’t wild growth. It’s… maintained.”
“Someone didn’t abandon this place. They let it continue.”
Lyra — First Reaction (Optional)
“It feels peaceful. That’s what worries me.”
“Places like this don’t ask you to leave.”
APPROACHING THE WELL — NON-COMBAT HAZARDS
Use 1–3 hazards total on the approach.
Each hazard follows:
Perception (Disadvantage)
On failure → Saving Throw
On failure → Apply 1 Marsh Mark
Hazard A — Grasping Roots
Read Aloud (Trigger):
Thick roots coil just beneath the surface, shifting as you move — not striking, just adjusting.
Save: STR or DEX
Failure: Brief restraint or slowed movement
Eldrin (if a PC fails):
“It adjusted to you. Like it expected that step.”
Hazard B — Sorrow Mists
Read Aloud:
A low mist clings to the ground, cool and familiar — like rain after a long night.
Save: CON or WIS
Failure: Disadvantage on next check or attack
Lyra (quietly):
“I almost forgot why we’re here.”
Hazard C — Echoing Ground
Read Aloud:
Your footing shifts — not slipping, just… wrong. The ground doesn’t match your stride.
Save: WIS
Failure: Movement subtly redirected
SOCIAL BEAT — THE LOST
Read Aloud
Figures stand waist-deep in the marsh, unmoving.
They breathe. They blink.
When they speak, their voices are calm — relieved.
What they say:
“It doesn’t hurt anymore.”
“I remember leaving once. I don’t remember why.”
“Why would I go back?”
They do not fight.
 They do not flee.
 They do not ask for help.
NPC Reactions
Eldrin
“They’re not trapped.”
“They chose this.”
Lyra
“Choosing comfort isn’t the same as choosing safety.”
(Later, quieter) “But I understand why they stay.”
THE RITUAL WELL
Read Aloud — First Sight
Stone terraces descend into a circular basin, each step worn smooth by time and care.
The water here is lower, slowly draining away, as if the ground itself is making room.
Roots curl back from the stone, deliberately, leaving the center untouched.
No attribution.
 No explanation.
TRANSITION POINT 1
➤ SWITCH TO BATTLE GUIDE: WELL GUARDIANS
Trigger:
Stepping onto the stone perimeter
Investigating the artifact directly
Read Aloud (or paraphrase):
The water ripples for the first time.
Shapes pull themselves free of the marsh — bone, root, and memory held together by stillness.
They do not rush you.
They wait.
MARSH MARK PAYOFF — GUARDIAN BATTLE
During the Well Guardian fight only:
At Initiative Count 20 (Each Round)
Each PC with 1+ Marsh Marks makes a Strength check
Fail: Movement speed is halved until end of next turn
Success: No effect
Flavor:
The ground tightens where it remembers you.
Optional escalation:
If 3+ Marks total, guardians gain advantage on their first grapple attempt
POST-GUARDIAN FALSE RESOLUTION
Read Aloud
As the last body collapses into the water, the marsh goes still.
No more movement.
 No more resistance.
The well lies quiet — open.
Let them heal.
 Let them breathe.
 This calm is intentional.
NPC Quotes
Eldrin
“That was it. Whatever was holding this together… it’s gone.”
Lyra
“If we’re careful, maybe we can end this without making it worse.”
They are wrong.
TRANSITION POINT 2
➤ SWITCH TO BATTLE GUIDE: ARTIFACT MANIFESTATION
Trigger:
Artifact is touched
Artifact is removed
Artifact is magically targeted
Read Aloud:
The artifact pulses — not violently, but urgently.
The water drains faster.
Roots pull away completely.
Something is trying to fix what should not be fixed.
BRANCH CONTEXT (FOR MANIFESTATION ONLY)
Branch A — No NPC Died
Undead manifestations are indistinct
Mercy misapplied broadly
No personal betrayal
Branch B — Eldrin Died
Eldrin is raised, calm and incomplete
Accepts this state as practical
Branch C — Lyra Died
Lyra is raised briefly, visibly wrong
Eldrin realizes immediately that this should not exist
BOSS DEFEATED — CUTSCENE & AUTO-ATTUNEMENT
Read Aloud (Cutscene)
The marsh exhales.
Roots loosen.
 Water settles.
The artifact grows warm — then heavy.
Before anyone can react, it shifts.
Not claimed.
Assigned.
Attunement (Automatic)
Artifact auto-attunes immediately
No roll, no choice, no reassignment
Choose the PC who feels narratively right
Describe to that PC:
The weight lifts something you didn’t realize you were carrying.
It feels easier to breathe.
 Easier not to care.
BRANCH-SPECIFIC AFTERMATH
If Lyra Died — Eldrin Breaks
Read Aloud:
Eldrin doesn’t move when the marsh settles.
His eyes stay fixed on where Lyra stood.
Eldrin Quotes:
“You decided what was acceptable.”
“You used her to prove a point.”
“That thing chose you. It should have been her.”
He may:
Storm off into the marsh
Turn on the party if pushed
Leave, vowing consequences
He is no longer a companion.
Other Branches
Eldrin (if alive & Lyra alive):
“Whatever that was… it’s not finished with us.”
Lyra (if alive):
“We didn’t stop it. We redirected it.”
“I don’t know if that’s better.”

SESSION ZERO — ASCENDARIA
**A Player Primer for Adventurers Bound for Lunaryth**

**What Your Characters Know**
- Ascendaria is distant, sparsely mapped, and rarely visited without purpose.
- You begin knowing only two locations:
  - **Tide’s Rest** — a small port town for lodging and supplies.
  - **Lunaryth** — a major elven city of temples, libraries, and academies.
- The journey inland is assumed to be safe and straightforward.

**Your Party — Shared Start, Flexible Relationships**
- You all arrive on the same ship bound for Tide’s Rest.
- You can decide if you already know each other or just met.

**What You Do Not Know (On Purpose)**
- Other settlements, landmarks, or regional names.
- Dangers, mysteries, or supernatural events.
- NPCs beyond what you discover in‑game.

**Party Composition Notes**
A balanced party helps, but optimization is not required. Consider:
- Damage dealers
- Support/healing
- A durable frontline
- Utility (skills, spells, or knowledge)

**Character Creation Guidelines**
All official 5E classes and races are allowed.
Possible motivations for traveling to Lunaryth:
- Study or magical training
- Searching for lost family or roots
- Seeking work, trade, or refuge
- Curiosity about elven culture
- Starting over in a new land
- Pilgrimage or personal mission
- Escaping trouble elsewhere

**Closing**
Your story begins on the ocean — who you are, and why you travel, is entirely up to you.

(DM-Only • Never Shown to Players)
SERIS OVERVIEW
Role: Companion, Catalyst, Moral Fulcrum
 Core Question: Who does Seris become when everything is taken from her?
Seris’s fate is determined by two hidden counters and one optional flag.
1️⃣ BELIEF COUNTER — Selûne ↔ Shar
Tracks: Ideology, worldview, divine influence
 Start: 0 (Torn)
 Range: +6 (Selûne) → −6 (Shar)
BELIEF STATES
+6 or more: Strong Selûnite
+3 to +5: Lean Selûne
−2 to +2: Unstable
−3 to −5: Lean Shar
−6 or less: STRONG SHAR — PRE-ORDAINED
⚠️ PRE-ORDAINED RULE
If Belief ≤ −6 at any time:
Seris’s fate is locked
Redemption becomes impossible
Bond/Romance may delay betrayal, never prevent it
Her behavior changes immediately
Do not announce this.
MAJOR BELIEF SHIFTS
Comfort Seris after Mara’s death → +2
Encourage revenge → −2
Moonfall ascension: concern for her → +2
Moonfall ascension: power at any cost → −2
Spare Elyndor Vaeloris → +3
Kill Elyndor Vaeloris → −3
Minor pressure (±1):
Mercy/compassion → +1
Cruelty/cynicism → −1
2️⃣ BOND COUNTER — Relationship with the Party

 Start: 0 (Neutral)

BOND STATES
+6 or more: Deeply Bonded
+3 to +5: Trusting
−2 to +2: Neutral
−3 to −5: Detached
−6 or less: Isolated

Support but push plot → +1
Leave her alone → −2
Treat grief as weakness → −3

Distance yourself publicly → −3

3️⃣ ROMANCE FLAG (OPTIONAL)

Stands apart

Takes risks for others

Radiant manifestations
Confidence replaces doubt
Openly challenges darkness
